Why NeuraFlash, Part of Accenture:

At NeuraFlash, Part of Accenture, we are redefining the future of business through the power of AI and groundbreaking technologies like Agentforce. As a trusted leader in AI, AWS, and Salesforce innovation, we craft intelligent solutions—integrating Salesforce Einstein, Service Cloud Voice, Amazon Connect, Agentforce and more—to revolutionize workflows, elevate customer experiences, and deliver tangible results. From conversational AI to predictive analytics, we empower organizations to stay ahead in an ever-evolving digital landscape with cutting-edge, tailored strategies.

We are proud to be creating the future of generative AI and AI agents. Salesforce has launched Agentforce, and NeuraFlash, Part of Accenture, was selected as the only partner for the private beta prior to launch. Post-launch, we’ve earned the distinction of being Salesforce’s #1 partner for Agentforce, reinforcing our role as pioneers in this transformative space.

Be part of the NeuraFlash, Part of Accenture journey and help shape the next wave of AI-powered transformation. Here, you’ll collaborate with trailblazing experts who are passionate about pushing boundaries and leveraging technologies like Agentforce to create impactful customer outcomes. Whether you're developing advanced AI-powered bots, streamlining business operations, or building solutions using the latest generative AI technologies, your work will drive innovation at scale. If you’re ready to make your mark in the AI space, NeuraFlash, Part of Accenture is the place for you.

As Solution Architect, Marketing Cloud Next, you will lead the functional solution design for Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next (MC Next) across our client engagements and act as the functional lead within NeuraFlash's MC Next practice. MC Next is built natively on the Salesforce core platform with Data 360, Flow and Agentforce, so the role combines marketing-platform fluency with data-architecture depth. You understand how marketing teams plan, segment, orchestrate and measure across channels, and you translate that into designs our Data 360, Agentforce and technical teams can build.

You will help lead MC Next solutions with key marketing, CRM, data and compliance stakeholders, and internally you will build the reference architectures, reusable patterns and enablement that let the rest of the practice deliver MC Next work with confidence.

You'll have the opportunity to:

  • Lead functional solution design for MC Next grounded in its Data 360 foundation: data model objects, ingestion from CRM and other sources, identity resolution, segmentation, and Actionable Lists, evaluating every requirement against native capability before recommending custom build.
  • Run discovery and design sessions with marketing operations, CRM, data, digital and compliance stakeholders to capture current-state platform capabilities, audience and data architecture, journey complexity, consent models and integration dependencies; present design decisions and trade-offs; and drive open questions to written closure with owners and dates.
  • Design campaign and orchestration architecture using Flow-based orchestration, messaging data sources, activation templates, landing pages and dynamic content for email, SMS and conversational channels, including Handlebars and AMPscript personalization where supported.
  • Design consent and compliance into the platform using the MC Next consent object model, consent records and landing-page consent capture, aligned to regional requirements such as CAN-SPAM, GDPR and CASL, so compliance is built in rather than bolted on.
  • Define platform setup and governance: edition and entitlement selection, Data 360 provisioning, Marketing Data Kit, Business Unit and Data Space structure, permission sets, CMS workspaces, and sending-domain authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and deliverability planning.
  • Shape agentic marketing solutions with our Agentforce specialists: marketing agents for campaign creation and audience generation, two-way conversational messaging, and predictive AI, with guardrails, approvals and measurement defined up front.
  • Lead migration and coexistence strategy for clients moving from Marketing Cloud Engagement, Account Engagement (Pardot), Marketo, Eloqua, HubSpot or similar platforms: wave sequencing, data and consent-state migration, journey and campaign translation to MC Next-native equivalents, and business-process equivalence checks at UAT.
  • Author and maintain the functional design: data model mappings, process flows, user stories with acceptance criteria and formal design sign-off artifacts, following NeuraFlash's Navigate Next delivery methodology and accelerators.
  • Translate the design for the build team (Technical Architects, Developers, Data 360 and Agentforce specialists), review configuration against spec, and support UAT and deployment gates.
  • Define what NeuraFlash owns versus what the client must provide (data access, SME availability, environment access, compliance approvals) and hold both sides to it.
  • Help build our MC Next practice: own reference architectures, capture reusable patterns from engagements, contribute to scoping calculators and SOW templates, and co-deliver enablement for the delivery team.
  • Support pre-sales as the MC Next subject-matter expert: discovery calls, solution shaping, demos and estimates (hours and scope; pricing stays with sales leadership), alongside our sales team and Salesforce marketing account teams.
  • Coach and mentor functional and technical team members on MC Next and stay current on Salesforce release changes across Marketing Cloud Next, Data 360 and Agentforce.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years in marketing automation consulting, marketing-technology solution architecture or business analysis, including hands-on delivery of enterprise marketing automation (Marketing Cloud Engagement, Account Engagement, or a comparable platform such as Braze, Marketo or Eloqua)
  • Hands-on experience with Marketing Cloud Next, or demonstrated ramp-up from Marketing Cloud Engagement or Account Engagement onto MC Next and Data 360 (the platform is new, so we weigh depth of adjacent delivery experience)
  • Working knowledge of Data 360 (Data Cloud) concepts: data model objects, ingestion, identity resolution, segmentation and activation, and how to troubleshoot data hygiene
  • Strong understanding of marketing consent and compliance requirements (CAN-SPAM, GDPR, CASL or similar) and how they shape data model, sharing and preference design
  • Experience designing multi-channel campaigns and orchestration (email, SMS, conversational or push), including personalization and content strategy
  • Practical knowledge of email deliverability: domain authentication, sender reputation and IP warm-up
  • Proven ability to lead discovery workshops, facilitate design decisions with senior marketing and IT stakeholders, and document them to sign-off
  • Experience working alongside Technical Architects and owning functional design through UAT and deployment
  • Ability to tie solution outcomes to business value (conversion, cost to serve, time to launch, attribution) through clear storytelling
  • Comfortable with flow-charting and data-modeling tools (for example Lucidchart) and with agile delivery
  • Willingness to travel to client sites as needed

Preferred Skills

  • Salesforce Certified Marketing Cloud Next Consultant; Data 360 Consultant; Agentforce Specialist; Platform Administrator; and an Application or Solution Architect credential
  • Marketing Cloud Engagement credentials (for example Email Specialist, Consultant) and Account Engagement Specialist, for migration and coexistence work
  • Hands-on experience with Flow Builder, including marketing flows and Agentforce actions
  • Integration experience with Salesforce CRM and external systems (REST APIs, MuleSoft or equivalent)
  • Experience with legacy-to-MC Next migrations, including subscriber, consent and journey migration
  • Experience in a regulated industry (health, financial services, nonprofit) where consent and PHI/PII handling shape marketing design
  • Experience with additional Marketing Cloud tools such as Personalization, Intelligence, Tableau Next or comparable reporting and attribution design

What can you expect in the interview process?

  • Recruiter screen (phone), 30 minutes. Introductory conversation to discuss the role and your experience.
  • Practice Lead Interview (video), 45 minutes. You'll talk through your career goals, relevant marketing platform work examples, and challenges you have overcome and the tools you used to get there.
  • Leadership interview (video), 30 minutes. You'll meet with a member of our leadership team.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

All employment decisions shall be made without regard to age, race, creed, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, citizenship status or any other basis as protected by federal, state, or local law. For details, view a copy of the Accenture Equal Opportunity Statement

What’s it like to be a part of NeuraFlash, Part of Accenture?

  • Remote & In-Person: Whether you work out of our HQ in Massachusetts, one of our regional hubs, or you're one of over half of our NeuraFlash, Part of Accenture Family who work remotely, we’re focused on keeping everyone connected and unified as one team.

Working closely with the VP of Accounting and Finance leadership, the Tax Manager develops and maintains tax processes, monitors changes in tax laws and regulations, supports audits and regulatory examinations, provides guidance on tax implications for business operations and organizational growth, and prepares the Company’s tax provisions. This position also identifies opportunities to improve tax efficiency, strengthen internal controls, and ensure compliance with all applicable reporting requirements. The ideal candidate is a collaborative leader with strong technical tax expertise, exceptional analytical skills, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while supporting a growing, multi-state organization.

Duties and Responsibilities

Tax Compliance

Tax Planning & Strategy

  • Ensure tax accounts within the general ledger are accurate and properly reconciled.
  • Assist with financial statement disclosures related to income taxes.
Audits & Regulatory Support

  • Partner with external tax advisors and auditors to support annual audits and compliance reviews.

Process Improvement & Internal Controls

  • Support implementation and optimization of software and tax reporting systems.
  • Maintain documentation to support compliance, audit readiness, and knowledge sharing.
Leadership & Collaboration

jobs.description:
Position Highlights

Location: This position is remote with occasional travel required to Oregon. Oregon-based candidates are preferred. The successful candidate will be hired by the CDC Foundation and will be organizationally located with Oregon Health Authority (OHA).

Salary Range: $90,000-$120,000, plus benefits. Individual salary offers will be based on experience and qualifications unique to each candidate.

Position Type: Grant funded, limited-term opportunity

Position End Date: October 30, 2028, with extension possible

Overview

The CDC Foundation is seeking a Project Manager to lead project management efforts for the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Policy & Programs team at the Oregon Health Authority, ensuring cohesive planning and execution of team priorities through high-level coordination and oversight. The Policy & Programs Project Manager will serve as a senior operational strategist, developing and managing the project schedule for the five program initiatives and three funding pathways, tracking key actions and decisions of Initiative Leads, guiding Grant Coordinators, and collaborating with the Program Manager to ensure appropriate cross-functional alignment within the program and elevation of risks and issues to program leadership. They will provide collaborative partnership to the Policy & Programs Senior Analyst, both of whom work with the Deputy Director of Policy & Programs to lead the team ensuring strategic alignment and efficient operations.

This position drives continuous process improvement across the Policy & Programs team, enhancing efficiency, consistency and alignment across the five program initiatives and three funding pathways. They oversee intra-initiative efforts as well as cross-functional collaboration by managing key meetings and team communications; maintaining integrated implementation schedules and deliverable tracking systems; directing the development process and dissemination of program materials; and ensuring consistent, transparent information flow across program initiatives and up to program leadership. The Policy & Programs Project Manager plays a critical role in strengthening program effectiveness by optimizing internal administrative and operational processes, applying advanced project management methodologies to improve organizational performance, accountability and cross-team coordination of complex requests for grant proposals and subsequent management of hundreds of grants and contracts that will total almost $1B over five years. This role also mentors project staff responsible for grant coordination and contributes to strategic planning and decision-making.

The position works in close partnership with the Operations Project Manager, the Program Affairs & Communications Project Manager, the RHTP Program Manager and RHTP leadership to ensure that program activities are strategically aligned, well-documented and progressing in accordance with CMS guidelines, timelines and priorities—supporting overall program and CMS coherence, impact and operational excellence. The Policy & Programs Project Manager will ensure the teams of subject matter experts and grant coordinators responsible for managing these funds remain in alignment with one another and with the broader Program, driving towards effective completion of federal milestones.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Leads strategic project management efforts overseeing planning, execution and coordination of complex program activities across the RHTP program’s three funding pathways, five initiatives and associated teams of grant coordinators.
  • Designs and manages integrated project frameworks, including detailed workplans, schedules and tracking systems to monitor timelines, milestones, interdependencies and deliverables for teams of subject matter experts designing and implementing the request for grant proposals and subsequent systems for managing approximately 100 grants and contracts per year.
  • Designs and executes meeting structures, agendas, materials and follow‑up tracking to support consistent cross‑team alignment and execution.
  • Builds and maintains detailed project plans using advanced tools such as Smartsheet to monitor daily tasks, key deadlines, dependencies and milestones.
  • Drives cross-functional alignment and communication, facilitating collaboration among diverse impacted parties to ensure shared understanding of priorities, proactive issue resolution and consistent progress toward program goals.
  • Synthesizes and delivers executive-level reporting, including dashboards, performance summaries and strategic insights to inform leadership decision-making and highlight key risks, achievements and upcoming milestones.
  • Oversees planning and execution of internal and external engagements, ensuring strategic alignment of agendas, materials and follow-up actions with program objectives and impacted party’s expectations.
  • Leads the design, implementation and continuous refinement of advanced project management processes, tools, templates, and workflows.
  • Conducts high-level analysis of RHTP operational systems, identifying structural gaps, inefficiencies and communication challenges, and drives the development and execution of improvement strategies that strengthen program performance.
  • Champions and institutionalizes standardized project management practices, guiding initiative teams in adopting shared tools, methodologies and reporting structures to improve coherence, accountability and cross-team coordination.
  • Develops, maintains and governs comprehensive process documentation, ensuring clear guidance for onboarding, knowledge transfer and sustainability of Policy & Programs operational systems across the five-year grant period.
  • Leads proactive identification, assessment and monitoring of program level risks, issues and dependencies.
  • Oversees the development and governance of comprehensive risk and issue management systems.
  • Directs the creation, implementation and tracking of mitigation strategies, working closely with the Program Manager, program leadership and initiative teams to ensure timely resolution and reduction of risk exposure.
  • Evaluates and advises on the implications of scope changes, timeline shifts and resource adjustments, providing strategic recommendations to maintain alignment with RHTP objectives and CMS requirements.
  • Perform other duties as assigned related to Rural Health.

Qualifications and Necessary Skills:

  • Master’s degree in public health or related field from an accredited college or university required (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
  • Minimum of 10 years leading complex projects or programs, with project management as a core responsibility.
  • Proven ability to scope, estimate and allocate resources for multifaceted initiatives with interdependent deliverables.
  • Advanced experience with project scheduling, risk management and coordinating workflows across diverse teams.
  • Experience creating, maintaining and regularly utilizing project trackers within enterprise project management tools to monitor project activities, deliverables, timelines, milestones and progress; Smartsheet experience preferred.
  • Demonstrated leadership in project or program management, ideally within a healthcare-related organization.
  • Strong capability in evaluating organizational systems, monitoring performance and driving corrective actions or process improvements.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop executive-level presentations and comprehensive reports.
  • Understanding of Oregon’s healthcare landscape, with emphasis on rural health systems and related challenges preferred.
  • Highly skilled in organizing, prioritizing, and managing multiple concurrent activities, timelines and impacted or interested party needs.
  • Ability to set long-term strategic objectives and define the plans and actions required to achieve them.
  • Skilled in identifying operational issues and leading efforts to design and implement process improvements.
  • Experience applying regulatory knowledge and sound judgment to ensure compliance with laws, standards and organizational policies.

Special Note

This position requires the operation of a motor vehicle as a component of the job responsibilities and duties. In adherence with CDC Foundation’s Driver Safety Motor Vehicle Policy (“Policy”), offers for employment for this position require the Applicant to provide authorization to the CDC Foundation to conduct a Motor Vehicle Record (“MVR”) review both pre-employment and also annually post-employment while in this position. Additionally, if an offer of employment is accepted, employees in these positions must possess and maintain a valid driver's license in their state of residence, self-report motor vehicle violations/convictions, and provide proof of acceptable insurance coverage with mandatory minimum coverages as set forth within the Driver Safety Motor Vehicle policy. All offers of employment and continued employment for this position are contingent upon meeting all minimum qualifications of this Policy.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, mental or physical disabilities, veteran status, and all other characteristics protected by law. We comply with all applicable laws including E.O. 11246 and the Vietnam Era Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974 governing employment practices and do not discriminate on the basis of any unlawful criteria in accordance with 41 C.F.R. §§ 60-300.5(a)(12) and 60-741.5(a)(7). As a federal government contractor, we take affirmative action on behalf of protected veterans.

The CDC Foundation is a smoke-free environment .

Relocation expenses are not included .

About the CDC Foundation

The CDC Foundation is an independent nonprofit authorized by Congress to mobilize philanthropic partners to support the public health system, including the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in preventing and responding to threats to health. In this role, we are focused on one priority: building catalytic, flexible and impactful partnerships—with corporations, philanthropies, individuals and organizations—to help improve the health and lives of people in all communities, everywhere. jobs.description:
The Design Systems Lead oversees the ongoing development of Discovery Education’s design systems and helps streamline the process from design to development. This role sits at the intersection of design and engineering, responsible for unifying our existing systems (Atlas and Nebula) into a scalable architecture while modernizing how our teams design, prototype, and deliver product experiences.

By aligning designers and engineers around shared infrastructure, this role improves collaboration, reduces duplication, and enables faster, more consistent product development across our ecosystem.

In This Role You Will:

Design System Architecture & Governance

  • Audit and evaluate existing design systems (Atlas and Nebula) to identify overlaps, gaps, and opportunities for consolidation.
  • Lead the evolution toward a unified, scalable design system architecture supporting multiple products and platforms.
  • Define standards for component governance, lifecycle management, and system documentation.
  • Implement a clear governance model (standards, contribution workflow, component lifecycle, documentation expectations, and ownership) to drive consistency and adoption.
  • Establish flexible system structures that allow components to adapt across products and experiences.
  • Own and maintain a unified design system direction (roadmap and decision-making) that consolidates and/or rationalizes Atlas and Nebula over time.

Design–Engineering Integration

  • Serve as the primary liaison between design and engineering teams for design system development.
  • Partner with engineers to ensure components translate efficiently from design into production code.
  • Align design and development workflows to reduce duplication and improve implementation quality.
  • Establish and maintain a design-to-engineering workflow that supports efficient implementation (libraries, tokens, specs, and collaboration practices).

Workflow Modernization & Tooling

  • Research and implement tools that improve design system development and front-end collaboration.
  • Explore emerging technologies, including AI-assisted design and development tools, to improve efficiency and scalability.
  • Introduce processes that enable faster prototyping and reduce friction between design and engineering teams.

Product Collaboration

  • Participate in product kickoff discussions with Product Design, Product Management, Curriculum, and Engineering.
  • Evaluate new initiatives through the lens of design system scalability and platform consistency.
  • Determine which patterns and components should become part of the shared system versus remaining product-specific.
  • Create enablement mechanisms that drive adoption (guidance, office hours, training) and build strong working rhythms with product teams.

Measurement & Continuous Improvement

  • Track design system adoption and metrics across teams and products.
  • Measure the impact of system implementation through metrics such as development efficiency, component reuse, design consistency, and team satisfaction.
  • Continuously refine system governance and workflows based on product and organizational needs.
  • Report regularly on outcomes (adoption, reuse, consistency, and delivery efficiency) and drive continuous improvement based on feedback and data.

Core Competencies for Success:

  • Manages complexity: Makes sense of overlapping systems (Atlas/Nebula), competing platform needs, and technical constraints to define a scalable design-system architecture and governance model.
  • Collaborates: Builds strong partnerships across Product Design, Engineering, Product Management, and Curriculum to align on standards, drive adoption, and reduce duplication.
  • Communicates effectively: Translates between design and engineering—creating clear documentation, decision records, and guidance that enables consistent implementation.
  • Tech savvy: Applies strong design system and front-end workflow knowledge (tokens, accessibility, tooling) to modernize practices and improve implementation quality.
  • Drives results: Establishes measurable goals for system adoption and impact (reuse, consistency, efficiency, satisfaction) and iterates based on data and stakeholder feedback.

Credentials and Experience:

  • 8+ years of experience in design systems, front-end (or design technology), or design-to-engineering workflows, with demonstrated impact on shipped products.
  • Proven ability to lead the strategy, architecture, and governance of a multi-product design system (standards, component lifecycle, documentation, contribution model, and adoption).
  • Strong cross-functional influence with the ability to align designers, engineers, and product partners around shared standards, tradeoffs, and roadmap priorities.
  • Deep knowledge of design system foundations, including design tokens, accessibility standards, responsive patterns, and modern design tools (e.g., Figma libraries, prototyping), plus familiarity with front-end frameworks and version control workflows.
  • Experience defining success metrics (adoption, reuse, quality, delivery efficiency) and using data and feedback to iterate on system direction and team workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor and enable others (designers and engineers) through documentation, office hours, playbooks, and training to scale best practices across teams.
  • Comfortable operating with autonomy in ambiguous problem spaces, breaking down complex work, communicating recommendations, and driving decisions with senior stakeholders.
  • Legal right to work in the United States.

This role is designed to be remote. The hiring range for this position is between $157,450 - $174,900 annually, however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and location. Additionally, this position is eligible for an Annual Bonus.

jobs.excerpt: Structural Integrity Associates, Inc.  (SIA) seeks a Pipe Stress Analysis Engineer with a strong foundation in the design, analysis, and evaluation of piping systems governed by ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section III, Division 1, and ASME B31 pressure piping codes.
jobs.description:
Structural Integrity Associates, Inc. (SIA) seeks a Pipe Stress Analysis Engineer with a strong foundation in the design, analysis, and evaluation of piping systems governed by ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section III, Division 1, and ASME B31 pressure piping codes. The successful candidate will perform and review piping stress, fatigue, flexibility, and dynamic analyses supporting operating plant assessments, system modifications, license renewal, power uprates, legacy analysis conversions, and advanced reactor designs.

This position supports our Nuclear Business Unit and contributes to projects involving thermal fatigue, vibration, seismic qualification, high-temperature service, degraded-condition evaluations, and fitness-for-service of piping and components. The ideal candidate is analytically strong, detail-oriented, adaptable to both modern and legacy piping analysis methods, and eager to learn from industry leaders who helped develop the ASME Code methods used today.

Primary Responsibilities:
  • Perform and review piping stress, flexibility, fatigue, and support-load analyses in accordance with ASME Section III, Division 1, including Subsections NB, NC, ND, and NF, and applicable ASME B31.1 Power Piping and ASME B31.3 Process Piping requirements.
  • Develop and evaluate load cases and combinations for pressure, deadweight, thermal expansion, seismic, vibration, water hammer, relief-valve thrust, and other static and dynamic loads in nuclear, fossil, and industrial applications.
  • Build, modify, troubleshoot, and independently check piping models using commercial and legacy analysis software, including AutoPIPE, CAESAR II, PIPESTRESS, ME101, ANSYS, or comparable tools.
  • Evaluate piping flexibility, equipment-nozzle loads, pipe supports and restraints, thermal transients, thermal stratification, vibration, and fatigue life.
  • Develop calculation packages, design reports, engineering justifications, and technical recommendations supporting new designs, plant modifications, operability, or continued operation.
  • Support failure evaluations, wall-thinning assessments, flaw evaluations, and fitness-for-service analyses for degraded piping and components.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, including materials, metallurgy, chemistry, finite element analysis, vibration, fracture mechanics, and plant engineering, to develop integrated solutions.
  • Prepare technical documentation, present results in client meetings, support field activities as needed, and contribute to proposals and scope development for new work.
  • Contribute to internal tools, automation scripts, calculation templates, process improvements, and best-practice guidance for piping analysis and integrity evaluations.
Required Skills/Qualifications:
  • B.S. in Mechanical or Civil Engineering; M.S. preferred.
  • 3 to 10 years of experience performing piping stress, flexibility, fatigue, or dynamic analysis in power generation, nuclear, process, or industrial facilities.
  • Working knowledge of ASME Section III, Division 1 piping design and analysis rules, particularly Class 1, 2, and 3 requirements under Subsections NB, NC, and ND, or demonstrated experience with ASME B31.1 and/or ASME B31.3.
  • Proficiency with one or more commercial piping analysis programs, such as AutoPIPE, CAESAR II, PIPESTRESS, or ANSYS, and the ability to interpret, verify, and clearly communicate complex analysis results.
  • Understanding of piping layout and flexibility, support and restraint behavior, equipment interface loads, thermal transients, vibration, and dynamic response.
  • Strong engineering judgment, problem-solving ability, communication skills, and technical writing capability.
  • Ability to work independently, review the work of others, and collaborate effectively within cross-disciplinary project teams.
  • U.S. citizenship or permanent residency required for certain nuclear projects.
Desired Skills/Qualifications:
  • Experience supporting nuclear plant design, operating plant modifications, license renewal or subsequent license renewal, power uprates, or advanced reactor programs.
  • Experience analyzing high-temperature piping systems, including service temperatures above 800 degrees F.
  • Experience with legacy piping models, software, and plant design bases, including the ability to interpret or convert models developed in programs such as ME101 or earlier versions of PIPESTRESS.
  • Familiarity with fracture mechanics, fatigue monitoring, environmentally assisted fatigue, thermal stratification, or fatigue evaluation methods.
  • Exposure to vibration field testing, flow-induced vibration diagnostics, operating deflection shape analysis, or troubleshooting of dynamic piping response.
  • Understanding of fitness-for-service methodologies, including API 579-1/ASME FFS-1, and familiarity with nuclear QA programs and industry guidance such as 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, EPRI, ASME, and WRC publications.
  • Experience with, or demonstrated interest and ability in, performing detailed finite element analysis and local stress evaluations of piping and piping components.
  • Licensed Professional Engineer (P.E.) in one or more U.S. states

Pay Range:
The expected annual salary range for this role $90,240 - $153,800 in San Jose, CA; $77,440 - $130,100 in Denver, CO; and $78,320 – $121,100 in Charlotte, NC. Exact pay will be commensurate with experience, qualifications, and location.

Application Deadline:
This position will remain open until filled. Applications will be reviewed on a continuous basis. To ensure full consideration, applicants are encouraged to submit their applications at the earliest opportunity.

Export Control Notice:
Certain positions at SIA may require access to information and technology which is subject to Export Administration Regulations 15 CFR 730-774, including those of the US Department of Energy (DOE) in 10 CFR 810 and Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) 10 CFR Part 110. Hiring decisions for such positions must comply with these regulations and may result in SI limiting its consideration of foreign nationals who are citizens of countries that are not on the DOE’s Generally Authorized Destinations List: .

SIA is an engineering consulting firm serving various industries including Nuclear Power, Energy Services, Pipeline Integrity, and Critical Infrastructure. Join a team of internationally recognized experts in a culture based on knowledge, excellence, and respect for one another. Our employees are members of a distinct community of internationally respected professionals committed to quality, engineering innovation and a shared goal of building a safer world.

Why Work at SIA?
SIA offers a competitive salary and performance-based bonus program. Our retirement benefits include a Traditional 401k, Roth 401k, and an employer match. To help employees maintain a work-life balance, SIA also offers various paid time off including vacation, floating holidays, sick time, and parental leave.

Job Overview

Welo Global is hiring an SDET (Software Development Engineer in Test) to bring deep technical rigor to middleware-layer testing. This role requires strong technical expertise across gRPC-Web, Proto3, HTTP/2, JSON-RPC/REST, proxy-based traffic inspection, and API scripting. The primary responsibility is to observe and reconstruct the network interactions generated by the onboarding UI, including request/response structures, schemas, headers, identifiers, Enums, and client-injected parameters. This is primarily an API/network analysis and evidence-generation role rather than a conventional UI automation or regression-testing role. The resource will produce sanitized network evidence and controlled, benign tracer replay scripts for downstream backend validation.


Project Details

Title: SDET - API/Middleware
Rate: $9.50/hr
Start Date: 19th October
Duration: 5 Weeks
Commitment: 35 Hours per Week
Location: India (Remote)
Job Type: Freelance

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain automated API test suites covering gRPC-Web, Proto3, HTTP/2, and JSON-RPC/REST based services
  • Export clean, sanitized HAR/network evidence while maintaining traceability between UI actions and corresponding network requests.
  • Map relevant schemas, headers, identifiers, routing information, and client-injected parameters.
  • Use proxy tools such as Mitmproxy, Charles Proxy, and browser DevTools to inspect, intercept, and validate network traffic between client and server
  • Develop and maintain API automation scripts using Python, Postman, and cURL for functional and regression testing
  • Analyze protocol-level request/response behavior to identify defects related to serialization, encoding, and transport
  • Inspect and validate request payload structure, including system-level headers (e.g., auth tokens, routing identifiers) and internal/hidden parameters, ensuring correct handling under both valid and malformed conditions
  • Collaborate with backend and middleware engineers to define testable contracts and edge-case scenarios
  • Continuously improve test automation frameworks for reliability, speed, and maintainability
  • Document technical findings, automation coverage, and known protocol-level limitations

Required Qualifications

  • Strong hands-on expertise of 3-5+ years with gRPC-Web, Proto3, HTTP/2, and JSON-RPC/REST protocols
  • Proficiency with proxy/traffic inspection tools including Mitmproxy, Charles Proxy, and browser DevTools
  • Solid scripting/programming skills in Python, with practical use of Postman and cURL for API automation
  • Experience designing and maintaining automated test suites for middleware or API-layer services
  • Working understanding of API request structure, including headers, auth tokens, and internal/system parameters, and how to test for their correct handling
  • Understanding of software engineering practices as applied to test automation (version control, CI integration, code review)
  • Strong debugging skills at the network/protocol level
  • Experience analysing browser-generated network traffic and reconstructing API behaviour is strongly preferred.
  • Experience with HAR analysis, API schema reconstruction, or controlled API replay is strongly preferred.
  • Ability to work within approved staging/test environments and follow defined data-handling and test-authorization requirements is required.

Right now, a dedicated team of Registered Nurses are working overnight from home, providing clinical assessment, triage and health advice to people across Australia.

It’s a different way to use your nursing experience. You’ll assess and support people across a broad range of health concerns, using your clinical experience to determine what care they need and how urgently they need it. One call might involve reassuring a concerned parent, while the next could require you to identify clinical deterioration, assess risk or determine that urgent medical care is needed.

Your experience and clinical judgement will be at the heart of what you do.

As one of our clinicians puts it:

“You are alone, but you are not. We have a really engaging team on Microsoft Teams and the Clinical Leads are incredibly supportive, they will guide you when you need it.”

“I'm constantly learning in this role, every shift builds my confidence and clinical judgement.”

  • Work from home anywhere in Australia
  • No commute to or from your overnight shift

  • Be part of a connected and supportive remote clinical team

Hours & Key Details

  • Full-time and part-time opportunities

You're an experienced Registered Nurse with strong clinical judgement who is comfortable assessing risk, making clinical decisions and communicating with people who may be anxious, uncertain or unsure what to do next.

Experience across mental health, adult and paediatric presentations or previous telehealth experience is highly regarded.

Paid Training

If overnight hours work for you and you’re looking for a different way to use your nursing experience, we’d love to hear from you.

Join a supportive team of experienced nurses, work from home, and use your clinical skills to make a meaningful difference to people across Australia.

Apply now to join our overnight Digital Health team.

Shape the future of a mature platform

Floworks is a leading specialty industrial supplier of flow control products, as well as a provider of technical solutions to the industrial and high purity end markets. Slater Controls is a leading distributor of valves, instrumentation, and automation equipment serving oil & gas, refining, power, and industrial customers across West Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona.

Job Information

The Valve Technical Services & Development Manager serves as a senior technical authority for control valves, valve automation, field service, and valve service operations. This role is responsible for the development of technician capabilities, provides advanced technical support to customers and internal teams, and supports the planning and startup of valve automation facilities in Phoenix, Salt Lake City, Denver, and other locations. The position works across locations to establish consistent technical practices, improve service quality, support complex field requirements, and help expand FloWorks/Ferguson valve automation & service capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as a senior subject matter expert for control valves, automated valve assemblies, pneumatic and electric actuators, positioners, instrumentation, diagnostics, repair, calibration, and testing.
  • Develop and deliver structured classroom, shop-based, and field training for valve technicians, sales personnel, and other associates.
  • Mentor technicians and establish practical competency standards, training plans, qualification criteria, and continuing training & development requirements.
  • Provide customer-facing technical training on control valve operation, maintenance, diagnostics, reliability, and valve automation.
  • Support troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, commissioning, startup, and field service for complex or critical valve applications.
  • Assist with the planning, layout, equipment selection, workflow design, safety considerations, and startup of valve automation and service facilities, initially including Phoenix, Salt Lake City, and Denver.

  • Review customer specifications, valve data, service histories, diagnostic results, and application conditions to recommend technically sound solutions.
  • Support development of work instructions, test procedures, inspection criteria, training materials, troubleshooting guides, and service documentation.
  • Assist with evaluation, onboarding, and technical assessment of valve technicians and other service personnel.
  • Represent the company professionally during customer visits, technical presentations, training events, plant outages, and field-service activities.

  • Experience leading field-service activities, technical teams, training programs, or multi-location technical initiatives strongly preferred.
  • Ability to diagnose complex valve and automation problems and communicate findings clearly to technicians, customers, sales teams, and leadership.

jobs.description:
PHILANTHROPY OFFICER

Department: Development

PLEASE NOTE: This position is open to clients Texas or Ohio.

JOB SUMMARY

The Philanthropy Officer builds and strengthens meaningful, long-term relationships with donors and prospects who have the capacity and affinity to make significant philanthropic investments in One More Child. Reporting to the Senior Director of Philanthropy, this role engages and grows an assigned portfolio within a specific region, engaging donors through discovery, meaningful engagement, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. The Philanthropy Officer develops individualized engagement strategies, builds a healthy pipeline of qualified prospects, and secures annual, capital, endowment, Comprehensive Campaign, and other strategic commitments in alignment with donor interests and One More Child’s priorities. Working collaboratively with the Executive Director of Philanthropy, Chief Advancement Officer and other organizational leaders, the Philanthropy Officer serves as a trusted ambassador for One More Child and invites donors into meaningful participation in the organization’s mission.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS

Donor Relationships & Portfolio Management

  • Manage an assigned portfolio of donors, building authentic, long-term relationships through meaningful engagement, discovery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Develop individualized relationship strategies based on each donor’s interests, passions, capacity, giving history, and relationship with One More Child.
  • Maintain consistent, thoughtful contact with donors through personal visits, calls, meetings, stewardship touchpoints, ministry experiences, events, and other meaningful engagement opportunities.
  • Listen to and understand donor interests and motivations, connecting them with opportunities to meaningfully advance the mission of One More Child.
  • Create meaningful donor experiences in partnership with regional, campus, program, and organizational leaders that deepen understanding of One More Child’s mission and impact.
  • Personally solicit and steward 5- and 6-figure gifts, multi-year commitments, and other philanthropic investments in collaboration with the Executive Director of Philanthropy and organizational leaders.

Prospect & Pipeline Development

  • Identify, engage in discovery, and cultivate prospective donors with the capacity and affinity to make significant investments in One More Child.
  • Build and maintain a healthy portfolio and pipeline, advancing qualified prospects through intentional relationship strategies and appropriate next steps.
  • Participate in regular portfolio and pipeline reviews with the Executive Director of Philanthropy and the Director of Development Strategy, using relationship intelligence to prioritize opportunities and strengthen donor investment.
  • Partner with the Director of Development Strategy to effectively use CRM data, metrics, analytics, and pipeline reporting to inform portfolio management and fundraising strategies.

Strategic & Campaign Fundraising

  • Develop and execute donor strategies that align donor interests and passions with One More Child’s strategic priorities and funding opportunities.
  • Participate in the Comprehensive Campaign and other strategic fundraising initiatives, cultivating and soliciting individual commitments for capital, endowment, annual giving, and other organizational priorities.
  • Collaborate with the Executive Director of Philanthropy, Chief Advancement Officer, Senior Vice President of Strategic Development, and other organizational leaders on significant donor strategies and solicitations.

Donor Communications & Collaboration

  • Provide donor insight and strategic direction for proposals, presentations, stewardship communications, and other materials supporting cultivation and solicitation.
  • Partner with the Director of Development Communications to develop compelling, donor-centered proposals and communications that connect donor interests with meaningful philanthropic opportunities.
  • Collaborate with Advancement, Communications, Programs, Partnerships, regional, and campus teams to ensure a coordinated and compelling donor experience.
  • Serve as an ambassador for One More Child, clearly and authentically communicating its mission, impact, vision, and opportunities for philanthropic partnership through events, personal visits, and speaking opportunities.

Performance & Professional Development

  • Meet established fundraising, portfolio, meaningful engagement, and pipeline goals while maintaining a focus on long-term donor relationships and sustainable philanthropic growth.
  • Maintain accurate and timely records of donor interactions, strategies, next steps, and portfolio activity in the organization’s CRM.
  • Continuously develop knowledge of One More Child’s programs, impact, strategic priorities, and funding opportunities to effectively engage and inspire donors.
  • Demonstrate integrity, discretion, professionalism, initiative, sound judgment, and commitment to ethical, relationship-based philanthropy.
  • Stay current with best practices in philanthropy and continually strengthen skills in donor engagement, discovery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Travel within assigned region regularly; at least annual visit to Headquarters in Lakeland.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Professional & Organizational Expectations

  • Pursues ongoing personal and professional growth to strengthen expertise and effectiveness in writing, proposal development, project management, and related areas through seminars, webinars, workshops, books, software, professional publications, and professional affiliations.
  • Brings creativity, initiative, strong organizational skills, and a high level of motivation to the role.
  • Demonstrates integrity, sound judgment, and maturity consistent with the organization’s core beliefs and values.
  • Demonstrates a positive attitude and genuine passion for the organization’s mission of providing Christ-centered services to children and families in need.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • N/A


REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, business, communications, marketing, public relations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Minimum of 3–5 years of experience in philanthropy, fundraising, development, sales, relationship management, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain authentic, trust-based relationships with individuals and organizations.
  • Experience cultivating relationships and securing financial support, investments, or other commitments from donors, customers, clients, or partners.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to listen effectively, ask thoughtful questions, understand motivations, and communicate compellingly with diverse audiences.
  • Ability to develop and execute individualized relationship strategies and manage multiple relationships, priorities, and opportunities with strong organization and follow-through.
  • Demonstrated initiative, sound judgment, professionalism, integrity, and discretion in working with individuals and confidential information.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with organizational leaders, colleagues, and cross-functional teams to advance shared goals.
  • Commitment to the mission, values, and Christian identity of One More Child.
  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly in assigned region for donor visits, meetings, ministry experiences, events, and other relationship-building activities.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • Demonstrated experience in major gifts, individual philanthropy, or relationship-based fundraising, preferably within a nonprofit or ministry environment.
  • Proven success personally cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding significant individual gifts, including multi-year commitments.
  • Experience securing six-figure or transformational gifts.
  • Experience participating in a Comprehensive, capital, or endowment campaign.
  • Established relationships within the philanthropic community, particularly within the assigned geographic region.
  • Experience managing a donor portfolio and using a CRM to track donor relationships, engagement, strategies, and next steps.
  • Experience using fundraising metrics, analytics, and pipeline information to inform donor strategies and prioritize opportunities.
  • Familiarity with relationship-based fundraising principles centered on discovery, meaningful engagement, and donor-centered philanthropy.

COMPETENCIES

  • Present oneself, both at and outside of work, in a manner keeping with One More Child’s Core Values of Humble, Hungry, Wise, and Called.
  • Relational Intelligence – Builds authentic, trust-based relationships by listening deeply, demonstrating genuine curiosity, understanding donor motivations, and creating meaningful connections.
  • Donor-Centered Philanthropy – Approaches fundraising as an opportunity to understand donor interests and passions and connect them with meaningful opportunities to advance the mission, rather than as a transactional exchange.
  • Strategic Thinking – Develops thoughtful relationship strategies, recognizes opportunities, prioritizes effectively, and balances long-term relationship building with measurable fundraising results.
  • Communication & Influence – Communicates with clarity, confidence, authenticity, and empathy; effectively articulates One More Child’s mission, impact, and philanthropic opportunities and inspires others to engage.
  • Initiative & Execution – Takes ownership, follows through consistently, manages competing priorities effectively, and turns relationship strategies and opportunities into meaningful action and results.
  • Collaboration & Stewardship – Builds strong partnerships with colleagues and organizational leaders, represents One More Child with professionalism and integrity, and demonstrates exceptional care in stewarding donor relationships and resources.

SPIRITUAL QUALIFICATIONS

  • It is the mission of One More Child to provide Christ-centered services to vulnerable children and struggling families. As stated in the Second Amended and Restated Articles of Incorporation, One More Child provides these services in a Christian context consistent with The Baptist Faith and Message (2000). Employees of One More Child commit to live in a manner that is not contrary to this foundational statement of faith.
  • Have had a personal conversion experience with Jesus Christ and been scripturally baptized.
  • Possess a sense of commitment to ministry through vocation.
  • Hold a sincere desire to seek God and His kingdom.
  • Demonstrate personal and devotional habits and practices such as Bible study, prayer, and daily meditation.
  • Be a member of a New Testament, evangelical church in the local community and attend regularly.
  • Engage in witness activities as a normal part of life.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

These physical requirements are not exhaustive, and One More Child may add additional job-related physical demands to these if the need arises. Corrective devices may be used to meet these physical requirements.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit and talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel. The employee is occasionally required to walk and reach with hands and arms. The employee must be able to operate a forklift. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

This job requires the ability to work in stressful conditions from time to time and remain focused for extended periods of time. The ability to lift up to 50 pounds (boxes, documents, and/or equipment) may be required on occasion.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment describes the conditions that an employee may encounter when performing their job duties, including but not limited to, the essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodation may be available to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these duties.

Job functions are performed in a normal office environment, with the option of hybrid/remote. Regular travel within assigned region and one to two visits per year to the headquarters in Lakeland are expected.

DISCLAIMER

This job description is not intended to be an all-inclusive list of the requirements of this position, but to describe the general nature of the job and provide a reasonable representation of its activities. Additional related work may be identified and assigned by the organization and included as an area of responsibility while assessing performance.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT

One More Child is committed to a workplace environment that encourages growth and respect for all current and prospective employees based upon job-related factors such as their educational background, work experience, and ability to perform the essential functions of a particular job. It is the policy and practice of One More Child to prohibit any form of discrimination or harassment based on statuses protected under federal, state, or local laws which are applicable to the organization. As a religious organization, One More Child provides services in a Christian context consistent with The Baptist Faith and Message (2000). Employees of One More Child commit to live in a manner that is not contrary to this foundational statement of faith.

jobs.description:
“Be part of a company that is influential and the standard for a rapidly evolving industry!”

WHO ARE WE?

RealTime eClinical Solutions is a Global Leader and rapidly growing SaaS technology company that provides comprehensive Software Solutions to the clinical research industry.

Our Vision is to reshape the global clinical research industry with innovative solutions that help advance medicine and save lives. Our cloud-based solutions are dedicated to solving complex problems and simplifying clinical research processes to be more organized, efficient, and cost-effective. We are based in San Antonio, TX, but are truly a remote and telecommuting company.

WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

Applicants must meet all minimum qualifications and required experience outlined in this posting to be considered for the position.

A dynamic Customer Health Supervisor to handle the day-to-day execution of the Customer Health operation across Tier 1 Customer Support and Tier 2 Product Health. This role ensures customer cases are progressing, service expectations are met, work is appropriately prioritized, and team members have the direction and coaching needed to consistently execute established processes.

The Supervisor is responsible for reinforcing a white-glove customer experience, ensuring customers receive timely, personalized, and meaningful communication with clear ownership and follow-through throughout the life cycle of the case.

The Supervisor serves as the frontline operational leader, translating the processes, standards, and priorities established by the Customer Health Manager into consistent daily execution

WHAT WILL YOU BE DOING?

  • Oversee daily operations across Tier 1 Customer Support and Tier 2 Product Health, ensuring appropriate coverage, workload distribution, and prioritization.
  • Monitor case queues, SLA performance, follow-up compliance, aging cases, and backlog health, taking action when cases are at risk.
  • Lead daily case and workload reviews to identify priorities, blockers, and cases requiring additional attention.
  • Provide day-to-day coaching, guidance, and support to team members to reinforce quality, accountability, and consistent execution.
  • Monitor case quality and ensure customer communications are timely, accurate, meaningful, and aligned with established standards.
  • Ensure established processes, workflows, escalation procedures, and documentation standards are consistently followed.
  • Identify cases requiring escalation and ensure they are properly triaged and handed off to the Customer Escalation Team for ongoing escalation management.
  • Ensure Tier 1 and Tier 2 work together effectively, with appropriate information and context flowing between customer support and product investigation.
  • Identify recurring operational issues, training needs, or workflow gaps and escalate those trends to the Customer Health Manager.
  • Support onboarding, training, and development of Customer Health team members.
  • Provide the Customer Health Manager with visibility into operational risks, performance gaps, workload concerns, and emerging customer issues.

WHAT DO YOU NEED?

  • 3+ years of experience in customer support, customer operations, technical support, or a similar customer-facing environment, with demonstrated experience providing day-to-day team leadership or supervision.
  • Experience working within the clinical research industry, with an understanding of clinical trial operations, workflows, and customer needs.
  • Experience supporting SaaS or cloud-based software solutions in a customer-facing environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver and reinforce a white-glove customer experience, with an emphasis on personalized communication, ownership, responsiveness, and follow-through.
  • Experience overseeing case or ticket queues, workload distribution, SLA performance, backlog health, and aging cases.
  • Experience providing coaching, feedback, and day-to-day guidance to team members to improve consistency and execution.
  • Strong ability to recognize customer risk and escalation triggers, appropriately triage issues, and engage the appropriate resources.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate professionally with both customers and internal stakeholders.
  • Strong organizational and prioritization skills with the ability to manage multiple customer issues, changing priorities, and time-sensitive work.
  • Demonstrated commitment to customer advocacy, accountability, attention to detail, and operational excellence.
  • Experience working with customer support and work-management platforms such as Salesforce, Zendesk, and Jira.
  • Intermediate proficiency with Microsoft Office and Microsoft 365 applications

jobs.description:
About zerohash

zerohash powers the infrastructure that allows businesses to seamlessly integrate digital assets into their products. Our APIs and embedded infrastructure enable brokerages, fintechs, banks, trading firms, and other financial institutions to build crypto and stablecoin experiences without having to build the underlying infrastructure themselves.

As we continue to expand our institutional trading and crypto infrastructure offerings, we are looking for an Integration Engineer to join our Implementation Services Team. In this role, you will lead the end-to-end technical execution and onboarding for high-value deals that are about to sign or have signed, focusing heavily on Central Limit Order Book (CLOB) FIX connectivity and adjacent crypto infrastructure products.

This role reports to the Head of Implementation Services.

About the Role

Integration Engineers at zerohash drive the critical bridge between contract signing and live production. Sitting at the intersection of complex financial technology, digital asset infrastructure, and customer delivery, you will be directly responsible for executing customer integrations from technical kick-off to successful go-live.

Your primary focus will be onboardings involving our CLOB FIX protocol engines and the full ecosystem of adjacent products that complement order matching, including:

• Account Funding & Payouts

• Crypto Deposits & Withdrawals

• Request for Quote (RFQ)

• Staking Infrastructure & Services

You will work directly with technical teams at institutional client organizations, guiding them through integration architecture, testing, API/FIX setup, and go-live readiness. Success in this role is measured by rapid time-to-production, smooth implementations, and building reliable, scalable integrations that drive immediate business volume.

This is a fully remote role for a candidate based in the US and/or Canada.

Responsibilities

• Lead Technical Implementation: Drive end-to-end integration workflows for deals nearing contract execution through go-live, serving as the lead implementation engineer.

• CLOB FIX & API Expertise: Act as the technical point of contact for clients integrating via CLOB FIX protocols as well as REST/WebSocket APIs for surrounding crypto workflows.

• Product Coverage: Guide institutional clients through configuring and implementing adjacent products, including Account Funding, Payouts, Crypto Deposits/Withdrawals, RFQ, and Staking.

• Technical Onboarding & Testing: Lead client engineering teams through sandbox environments, connection configuration, order-flow validation, edge-case testing, and production deployment.

• Troubleshooting & Debugging: Directly diagnose, debug, and resolve implementation blockiers, API errors, payload misconfigurations, and connectivity issues during the onboarding lifecycle.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, and Core Engineering teams to hand off client requirements seamlessly and accelerate feature additions needed for go-live.

• Implementation Tooling & Playbooks: Continuously optimize implementation playbooks, client integration documentation, and automated testing tools to shorten client onboarding timelines.

Requirements

• 3–5+ years of experience in Integration Engineering, Technical Implementation, Technical Onboarding, Solutions Architecture, or a similar technical client-facing role.

• Deep technical experience with FIX Protocol (FIX 4.2 / 4.4 / 5.0) in institutional trading, exchange, or market infrastructure environments.

• Hands-on proficiency with web APIs: Deep understanding of REST, WebSockets, JSON/HTTP, and distributed architecture patterns.

• Core Technical Skills: Hands-on experience with SQL and at least one programming/scripting language (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, or Java) for debugging, log parsing, and building test scripts.

• End-to-End Delivery: Proven track record of managing technical implementations from initial kick-off through production launch under tight timelines.

• Communication & Technical Delivery: Ability to effectively lead technical working sessions with client developers, system architects, and technical project managers.

• Problem-Solving: Strong analytical capabilities to troubleshoot real-time order-flow issues, ledger adjustments, and protocol discrepancies across complex multi-product environments.

Preferred Qualifications

• Domain Knowledge: Direct experience with Order Management Systems (OMS), Execution Management Systems (EMS), Central Limit Order Books (CLOB), or matching engine connectivity.

• Crypto Infrastructure Experience: Prior background implementing digital asset custody, crypto rails, deposit/withdrawal sweeping, yield/staking protocols, or fiat payout gateways.

• Institutional Trading Background: Experience working alongside prime brokers, proprietary trading desks, fintech brokers, or institutional crypto exchanges.

• AI & Automation: Experience using AI-assisted tools to accelerate learning, log analysis, code generation, and implementation troubleshooting.

Benefits

We believe a happy, motivated, and healthy team is the best way to succeed. We offer the following benefits:

  • Healthcare Insurance: zerohash covers roughly 100% of employee premiums as well as a portion of spouse/children (U.S. only)
  • Vision & Dental Insurance (U.S. only)
  • Chance to earn equity
  • Maternity & Paternity leave (after 6 months)
  • WeWork All Access Membership
  • WFH Yearly Stipend
  • L&D Yearly Stipend (after 6 months)

About zerohash

zerohash is the leading crypto and stablecoin infrastructure platform and the operating system for digital money, powering the next generation of financial services. Founded in 2017, zerohash enables banks, brokerages, fintechs, and payment companies to offer crypto trading, stablecoin payments, and tokenized assets without having to build or manage complex blockchain infrastructure on their own.

The zerohash platform supports three core pillars: Trade, Transact, and Tokenize. Through a single integration, customers can launch regulated crypto buy, sell, and custody services; enable 24/7 stablecoin-based funding, payouts, and settlement; and issue and manage tokenized assets with built-in compliance, risk controls, and reporting. By abstracting away technical, regulatory, and operational complexity, zerohash allows partners to treat digital assets as just another financial primitive: fast, programmable, and global.

zerohash is trusted by some of the world’s most recognized financial and consumer brands, including Interactive Brokers, Morgan Stanley, Stripe, Franklin Templeton, BlackRock, DraftKings, Gusto, Worldpay, Kalshi, One Pay, among others. Today, zero infrastructure supports millions of end users across brokerage, wealth, payments, and marketplace platforms globally.

The company is deeply regulated and compliance-first, operating across the U.S. and internationally with licenses and approvals that allow partners to enter crypto and stablecoins with confidence. zerohash has become a trusted partner for enterprises seeking to modernize financial products while meeting the highest standards for security, risk management, and regulatory oversight.

To date, zerohash has raised over $280 million in funding from a mix of leading venture firms and strategic investors, including Morgan Stanley, Interactive Brokers, SoFi, Point72 Ventures, Bain Capital Crypto, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and more.

zerohash has been featured in top-tier media outlets such as Bloomberg, CNBC, The Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, Reuters, Forbes, and CoinDesk, and its leadership team regularly contributes to global conversations on the future of payments, investing, and financial infrastructure.

At zerohash, we're building the infrastructure that makes digital money work securely, compliantly, and at global scale.

The zerohash Culture

All zerohash employees are guided by the following characteristics and core principles:

  • Independence/Ownership - An ability to work autonomously. Join zerohash, pitch ideas, and shape the work you do.
  • Passion - We are innovating quickly and challenging the status quo. We want you to think big, be creative and ​make a difference every day.
  • Collaborative - A good attitude and respect for others. We’re teammates, not co-workers. Everything we do is a shared success and equally a shared failure - we talk in terms of “we” not “me”.
  • Initiative - An ability and passion for learning and asking questions. We will champion you, challenge you and push you to achieve your best - and we expect you to do the same.
  • Empathy - An ability to listen, respect, and understand your co-workers, customers, and everyone you interact with no matter how different they are to you.
  • Adaptability - An ability to respond quickly. We are in a fast-paced industry and so we expect you to be creative when solving a new problem and comfortable under pressure.
  • Transparency - We believe that transparency is critical to empowering everyone to make the best decisions, both the company to its people and vice versa.
  • Integrity - Integrity creates trust. As both an organization collectively and as individuals, it is our most valuable asset.

Follow us

jobs.excerpt: About CircleCI EngineeringCI/CD has been solved.  Now it's being reinvented.
jobs.description:
About CircleCI Engineering

CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.

At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.

About the On-Prem Team

The On-Prem team ships CircleCI Server, our self-hosted CI/CD platform for customers who need to run everything inside their own infrastructure: regulated industries, air-gapped environments, and teams with strict data residency and compliance requirements. Our mission is to deliver an on-premises CircleCI that is secure, highly available, and easy to install, upgrade, and support.

Our team serves two kinds of customers: the organizations that run Server, and the CircleCI engineering teams whose services ship inside it. Beyond the product itself, we own the tooling and infrastructure that let those teams package, test, and release their services into Server and keep them current. As a Staff Engineer here, you'll care as much about the internal release experience as about making Server reliable and easy to operate for external customers.

What You'll Do

  • Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how we approach and solve problems.
  • Make shipping into Server easy for every team. Own the platform strategy, setting the technical direction for the tooling, test infrastructure, and release automation that CircleCI teams use to develop and maintain their services inside Server.
  • Give customers confidence installing, upgrading, and running CircleCI Server. Customers run Server in environments you'll never see. Make the install experience simpler and more predictable, upgrades safer, and day-to-day operation easier, starting with sensible defaults.
  • Own Server's foundation. You'll be responsible for everything from the Kubernetes infrastructure Server deploys into, to the tooling internal teams and customers depend on. That responsibility extends past your own code to the systems and teams around it.
  • Get operators from symptom to root cause fast. Standardize Server's observability on OpenTelemetry so it works with whatever platform each customer already runs. Build diagnostics that help operators, and the engineers supporting them, find the problem quickly. Partner with Support, Customer Engineering, and customers to find recurring issues and fix them at the source.
  • Connect engineering to the business. Partner directly with Product and Engineering Management to translate business goals into technical strategy. You understand the "why" behind the roadmap and use it to make tradeoffs.

What You'll Bring

  • A platform mindset. You default to building tools, frameworks, and systems that make other engineers more productive rather than solving each problem one-off. You've built internal platforms before and can talk about the leverage they created for the teams that used them.
  • AI-native engineering practices. You use AI tools daily and can speak to what you've built, where they changed your approach, and where they fall short.
  • Deep experience with Kubernetes and Helm. You've designed, deployed, and debugged production systems on Kubernetes. You know where the sharp edges are, especially in customer-operated environments (air-gapped, restricted network, unfamiliar cluster shapes).
  • Strong backend and systems foundation. 8+ years building production backend and infrastructure systems, with a history of taking accountability for outcomes. Strong in Go, with real experience in API design, data modelling, distributed systems, and operational tooling.
  • System design with business context. You make architecture decisions that span multiple systems and teams, weigh tradeoffs against business needs, and document your reasoning. You're the person others escalate to when the answer isn't obvious.
  • Technical leadership. You mentor engineers, give direct feedback on technical direction, and raise the quality bar across teams through how you engage in reviews and design discussions, not just what you ship.
  • Experience with on-premises or self-hosted software. You've shipped software that runs in someone else's environment (enterprise on-prem, self-hosted SaaS, or a distributed system installed by customers), and you understand how that constraint shapes your design choices, release process, and support model.

Sound Like You?

You believe the best platform work makes everyone else faster. You're energized by the challenge of building software that has to work in environments you can't see or control. You want to take a product customers depend on and make it dramatically easier to build, ship, and run, both for them and for the teams whose services live inside it. If that sounds like you, let's talk.

About CircleCI

CircleCI is the world’s largest continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform, and the hub where code moves from idea to delivery. As one of the most-used DevOps tools - processing more than 3 million jobs a day - CircleCI has unique access to data on how the most effective engineering teams work, and the tools to help software companies successfully leverage the power of AI into their commercial applications. Companies like Hinge, HuggingFace, and Samsung use us to improve engineering team productivity, release better products, and get to market faster.

Founded in 2011 and headquartered in downtown San Francisco with a global, remote workforce, CircleCI is venture-backed by Base10, Greenspring Associates, Eleven Prime, IVP, Sapphire Ventures, Top Tier Capital Partners, Baseline Ventures, Threshold
Ventures, Scale Venture Partners, Owl Rock Capital, Next Equity Partners, Heavybit, and Harrison Metal Capital.

CircleCI is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law.

How CircleCI Uses AI in Hiring

At CircleCI, people make our hiring decisions. We use technology to support our recruiting team so they can spend more time on what matters most: getting to know you.

Where we may use AI

  • Job descriptions and messaging: AI may help draft job descriptions and role-specific messaging so they are clear and accurate.
  • Application review: For some roles, we use an AI tool to review applications, including resumes and application responses, against criteria our hiring team sets for the role. The tool generates a fit score and summary to help recruiters organize and prioritize applications.
  • Interview notes: With advance notice, an AI note-taking tool may join interviews to record, transcribe, and summarize the conversation. This lets interviewers focus on talking with you. You will be told before each interview, and you may opt out at any stage by letting your recruiter know. If you opt out, the tool will not join, and your candidacy is not affected.
  • Outreach: AI may help draft candidate outreach and scheduling messages, which our team reviews before sending.

Our commitment

AI does not make hiring decisions at CircleCI. Our recruiters and hiring teams review candidates and make every decision to advance or reject an application. No candidate is rejected based solely on an AI score. We have tools and processes in place to test for bias and to review how these tools perform, and we adjust our approach as AI technology and the laws that govern it change.

Your choices

You can ask for human-only review of your application, opt out of AI interview note-taking, request an accommodation, or ask questions about how we use AI. Contact how we handle your data, including retention, see our Privacy Policy.
