jobs.description:
Who we are

Phorest started in 2002 on a busy salon reception desk as a simple text-reminder tool.

Today, we're a SaaS company and a trusted partner to over 155,000 hair, beauty and medspa professionals worldwide. Our all-in-one software and AI-driven tools help them manage bookings, take payments, market their services, grow their client base and get the best from their teams.

Everything we build helps the salon and medspa industry thrive.

We're also a Certified B Corp, and 25% of the company is owned by Phoresters. When the company grows, everyone has a stake in that.

The Opportunity

At Phorest, our Customer Success teams help thousands of salons, spas and medspas grow their businesses. We're looking for a Global Customer Success Domain Manager to help those teams work smarter, more consistently and at scale.

In this role, you'll lead a team that owns the processes, tooling and ways of working behind Customer Success across all our regions. You'll partner closely with regional leaders to understand what they need. Then you'll turn that into global solutions that improve retention, reduce churn, grow feature adoption and drive revenue performance.

You'll be the bridge between frontline regional needs and global strategy. The role combines people leadership, commercial awareness and deep operational expertise, with plenty of room to make your mark.

What You'll Do

Leading your team

  • Lead, coach and develop a team of experienced specialists, setting clear goals and supporting their growth.

  • Build an inclusive, collaborative, high-performing team culture that reflects Phorest's values.

  • Plan your team's capacity so you can deliver on the domain roadmap.

Driving revenue impact with regional teams

  • Partner with regional Customer Success leaders to understand their priorities, challenges and targets.

  • Help regions hit their goals on Net Revenue Retention (NRR), retention, expansion and customer adoption.

  • Prioritise initiatives based on customer value, commercial impact and operational efficiency.

Improving processes

  • Design, improve and standardise Customer Success processes across onboarding, adoption, upsell, feature activation and risk mitigation.

  • Create scalable workflows, frameworks and documentation that make teams more productive and improve the customer experience.

  • Drive global consistency while considering local market needs.

Owning Customer Success tooling

  • Own and improve the Customer Success tooling stack so teams can operate effectively at scale.

  • Partner with Product, Data and Engineering on system improvements and integrations that give better visibility of customer health, risk and revenue opportunities.

  • Work with Global Enablement so teams are trained and confident with new tools and best practices.

Boosting feature adoption and reducing churn

  • Track feature adoption across regions and work with Product and Onboarding to close gaps.

  • Use data and customer insight to understand why customers churn, and build improvements to prevent it.

  • Work with third-party partners to make setup smoother for new and upgrading customers.

Using data to keep improving

  • Define and track the KPIs that show whether process and tooling changes are working.

  • Build business cases and prioritisation frameworks for strategic initiatives.

Who You Are

You're highly collaborative, commercially aware and passionate about building operational solutions that help teams succeed. You thrive in complex global environments. You enjoy solving problems through process and systems thinking, and you're motivated by measurable business impact.

You have:

  • 8+ years' experience in Customer Success Operations, Revenue Operations, Customer Operations, Program Management or a related operational leadership role in SaaS or tech.

  • Experience leading and developing a team.

  • A track record of working with global or multi-regional teams and driving improvements in retention, expansion, adoption or scalability.

  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives with measurable business outcomes.

  • A strong understanding of Customer Success metrics, lifecycle management and commercial drivers.

  • Hands-on experience with Customer Success platforms, CRM systems, workflow automation and reporting tools.

  • Strong analytical skills and a data-driven approach to solving problems.

  • The ability to influence and communicate across all levels, adapting your style to different audiences.

Benefits

🏡 We're a remote-first company with a team spread across Ireland, the UK, the DACH region, North America and Australia. We believe great work comes from trust, so you'll have the flexibility to shape your working day around what works for you, your life and your team.

🌳 We grow our own timber! We provide dedicated Learning Days every year, a mentoring program, career coaching, development programs, and access to tools that help you build skills and shape your career.

🧘 Your wellbeing is important to us - we provide private healthcare, 2 Wellness Days, an employee assistance program.

🍼 We care for your family and provide Enhanced Maternity and Paternity Benefits.

🦸‍♀️ We support the women who work in Phorest by offering 2 weeks' leave for fertility treatment, pregnancy loss, and menopause.

🏠 Moving house? Phorest employees get 3 moving days.

💰 As part of our Financial Wellbeing, we provide competitive compensation, an Employee Share Purchase Scheme, Pension, Life Assurance, and Income Protection.

🚵🏿 We help you travel by providing a bike-to-work scheme as well as tax-saver transport tickets.

The details may vary slightly by country; your Talent Acquisition Partner will walk you through what applies where you're based.

Phorest is an equal opportunity employer. For this position, flexi-time and working from home is possible. We are also open to remote work. Get in touch to ask for more information or to chat about your future with Phorest!

Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other marginalised folks tend to only apply when they check every box. So if you think you have what it takes, but don't necessarily meet every single point on the job description, please still get in touch. We'd love to have a chat and see if you could be a great fit.

jobs.title: Security Engineer
jobs.excerpt: We're on the lookout for a Security Engineer to join Nucleus' Information Security team, to help ensure that we are secure by design.
jobs.description:
We're on the lookout for a Security Engineer to join Nucleus' Information Security team, to help ensure that we are secure by design.

About the role

The Security Engineer supports the delivery of Nucleus’s technology and business change agendas by translating security requirements into practical, working controls. Security requirements are set within the Information Security function; the Engineer is the person who turns them into designed, implemented and validated controls. This includes reviewing technical designs against those requirements, building and configuring the controls, embedding them into our operations, and evidencing that they work as intended. The Engineer works closely with teams across Nucleus, and with outsource partners involved in delivery, to land the right security outcome in each change.

The Information Security team aims make sure that Nucleus is a trusted partner to the firms and people we work with. Being able to demonstrate that our systems are secure, through a structured control environment, is a core component of building that trust. This role is critical to delivering that outcome: being the go-to contact for implementing security controls; being ‘hands on’ with their design and configuration; and validating that controls work as intended through technical assessment, identifying opportunities for continuous improvement. Where a control cannot be delivered as intended, this role is also about articulating the resulting risk clearly and pragmatically, so the accountable people can decide how to handle it. This is a proactive, build-and-assure role, distinct from a monitoring or alert-response function.

You’ll work with SMEs across Nucleus, you’ll ensure that new processes and controls are handed over to the relevant team, and that the Information Security Analysis team have suitable evidence to demonstrate that our risks are effectively managed.

Responsibilities
  • Apply security best practice in our change and development programmes, to ensure delivery is within our risk appetites.
  • Review technical designs against agreed security requirements, then design and implement the controls that meet them, following industry best practice and Nucleus standards.
  • Work with technical and delivery teams to produce and deliver remediation plans for identified vulnerabilities and control gaps, in line with Nucleus’ risk appetites.
  • Clearly communicate security risks where requirements cannot be fully met, so the business can make informed decisions on whether to accept, mitigate or remediate, and balance security with delivery.
  • Maintain systems and integrations that enable these controls.
  • Validate that delivered controls work as intended, and capture the evidence needed to demonstrate they are effective.
  • Coordinate on security controls within other members of the Nucleus Group, to ensure Nucleus has an end to end understanding of our exposures and capabilities.
  • Support Audit and Due Diligence activities to help demonstrate Nucleus’s capabilities.
  • Work with Security Operations and Analysis to adopt and maintain standards that ensure Nucleus continues to manage our security risks effectively.
  • Take responsibility in everything you do to deliver good outcomes for our customers
  • Positively demonstrate the Nucleus Smart, Heart and Courage values and behaviours
  • Ensure compliance with Code of Conduct at all times

About you

Your friends might describe you as ‘the methodical one’. You love to look at how everything fits together to see the bigger picture, identifying where things can go wrong, and putting pragmatic solutions in place to catch them before they happen.

You’ll enjoy working within a fast-paced environment that gives you the opportunity to multi-task within set deadlines. Professional with a positive outlook, you’ll take great pride in your ability to act on your own initiative and remain flexible in changing circumstances and priorities.

You’ll be confident navigating challenge and competing priorities, holding a technical position where the security outcome depends on it, and doing so constructively. You build influence through the quality of your reasoning rather than relying on authority, and you stay composed and evidence-led when your thinking is tested.

At Nucleus, we place real value in cultural contribution and diversity of thought. For this role we’re also looking for genuine technical depth, so while we wouldn’t expect every item below, we’d want you to bring a good number of them:
  • Exposure to recognised control frameworks, in particular the CIS Critical Security Controls, with an understanding of how frameworks like NIST SP 800-53 or the NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework benefit an organisation. You understand what these frameworks are for, not just that they exist.
  • Able to identify effective implementation and test plans, and deliver those through either in house capabilities or by working with external providers, and demonstrate how they help manage Nucleus’ risks.
  • An excellent communicator, able to discuss security effectively with areas of the business.
  • Solid, demonstrable Information Security experience, ideally including time in a regulated environment such as financial services.
  • Strong knowledge of IT, Infrastructure and Networking concepts.
  • Hands-on experience building and maintaining the systems and integrations that enable security controls.
  • Experience working with cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure and AWS, including operating and maintaining security controls and responding to findings from cloud security posture or workload protection tooling.
  • Able to weigh other people’s views, apply sound technical judgement, and provide constructive challenge where it is needed to manage our Information Security risks effectively.
  • Able to articulate security risk in clear, practical terms, helping stakeholders make informed decisions about accepting, mitigating or remediating, rather than presenting security as a blocker.
  • Ownership of tasks, attention to detail and following through to conclusion.
  • Ability to prioritise and remain agile with competing work demands.
  • Comfortable working independently on technical delivery, seeing work through to a validated, evidenced conclusion.
A little about us

Our purpose at Nucleus is to transform financial services and create better outcomes for our advisers and their clients. It is this purpose that drives everything we do. Whether you are working in a role that is client facing or not, you’ll need to be service obsessed to work here.

It’s a fast paced and exciting environment, and one where we believe you will get the chance to fulfil your potential and do work that really matters, to you and our clients. We believe in you having your own chunk of responsibility and being trusted to make things happen.
Nucleus’ culture is something our people believe sets us apart from other places they’ve worked. We think big, know our stuff and move at pace, but always empowering others along the way and breaking new ground to find better ways of doing things. We know that sometimes the right choice is not the easy one, so empowering each other and celebrating others' successes, as well as our own, is part of what makes us Nucleus #WeAreNucleus
Inclusion and diversity at Nucleus

As with most things in life, who cares, wins. We really care about inclusion.
For us this is not a box-ticking thing, it’s a commercial imperative. It isn’t about being PC. It’s about being future relevant and durable.

Find out more on our inclusion page

We’re proud to partner Stonewall and be a diversity champion for Scotland. This partnership demonstrates our ongoing commitment to diversity by providing an environment where everyone feels welcome, able to be their authentic self and do the best work of their life.

We offer a generous blend of benefits for the things that really matter to our people, including pension, bonus, enhanced parental leave, paid time off for emergencies, health and wellbeing initiatives and flexible working options.

  • Strong customer-facing communication and de-escalation skills.

  • Managed Service Provider (MSP) environments

  • Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BCDR)

  • Disaster recovery workflows

  • Infrastructure monitoring

  • Network or security appliances

  • Cloud infrastructure

  • Linux environments

  • Troubleshoot systematically rather than simply respond to alerts.

  • Identify the difference between an issue you can resolve independently and one that requires escalation.

  • Communicate calmly and clearly with customers during critical situations.

  • Provide useful technical context when escalating incidents.

  • Build deeper expertise in backup, recovery, and disaster recovery technologies over time.

  • Maintain a strong customer experience while meeting technical and SLA expectations.

Why Join Us?

This is an opportunity to work in a highly technical support environment where you can deepen your expertise in infrastructure, backup, networking, and disaster recovery while collaborating with experienced technical teams.

You’ll have the opportunity to take ownership of complex incidents, strengthen your Tier 3 troubleshooting skills, and contribute to a growing international support operation.

As a Software Engineer on our AI Systems team, you'll build the AI foundations and product experiences of Ledgy: the Ledgy Agent, the tools and skills it runs on, our MCP server, and the platform capabilities that let other teams embed AI safely in their domains. You'll collaborate with fellow engineers, product managers, and designers in a new and fast-moving product area where correctness matters as much as speed - our customers need equity data they can trust.

Location: We hire remotely across the UK, Spain, Germany, Poland, and Romania. For candidates based in London, we use a hybrid model with 2 days in the office per week.

The team you'll join:
AI Systems - Develops Ledgy's AI foundations and product experiences, from AI agents and AI-assisted workflows to the platform capabilities that help other teams embed AI safely in their domains. The team works in a new and evolving product area, balancing rapid iteration with reliable execution, evaluation tooling, and responsible automation.

What You'll Work On

Help build the future of how companies manage equity.

  • Ledgy Agent. You'll design and build the system behind our in-app agent, so equity administrators can do through AI what they do manually in the app today. Ledgy Agent takes real actions and runs real analysis on live equity data, like onboarding a stakeholder end to end, and administrators depend on its accuracy and observability. You'll design the tools, skills, context, and orchestration behind it, and how it decides to handle each request.
  • Ledgy MCP. Not everyone wants to open Ledgy to get things done. Our MCP server lets customers bring equity into the AI agents and tools they already use. You'll shape it alongside the in-app agent, so a capability built once works in both places, and you'll decide what we expose and how we keep it safe.
  • Measuring and improving the agent. You'll design and build the system we use to measure the agent's quality and learn from how customers use it: evaluations, tracing, and feedback from real conversations. You decide what "good" means for customers, how we measure it, and how what we learn changes what we build next.
  • Scaling. The Ledgy web application, the agent, MCP, and surfaces we haven't built yet all need the same capabilities. You'll design the foundations that let us build AI features once and reuse them everywhere, and that let other teams add AI to their domains without compromising correctness. You'll also design how it runs as usage grows: the backend infrastructure, cost, and latency behind the agent and MCP, and how we keep them reliable and observable.

You'll own real parts of this and have a say in where we invest. You'll also spend time with customers to see how administrators actually use the agent, and use that to decide what to build next.

You'll Thrive in This Role If You

Don't worry if you don't tick every box. These are the things that would make you an especially good fit.

  • You have 5+ years of experience working as a Software Engineer, with strong TypeScript/Node fundamentals across back end and front end
  • You've built and shipped agentic or LLM-based software to production, such as an agent, an assistant, or a chat product, and you've been the one running it. You've debugged failures in real conversations and kept cost and latency in check as usage and models changed.
  • You've designed the agent itself: tools and skills, context and prompt engineering, state, streaming, and the agent loop. You know at least one agent framework or runtime well and can say where it works and where it doesn't.
  • You improve these systems with evidence. Evals, regression sets, tracing, and feedback from real usage tell you whether a change helped, and you use them to decide what to do next.
  • You keep up with what the foundation labs and the wider community are learning about building agents. You try new techniques early and judge which ones make our product better and are worth adopting now, and which should wait.
  • You take part in deciding what we build. You read the data, talk to customers, and push for what you think matters most.

Our Tech Stack

We work in a TypeScript monorepo: React and Tailwind on the front end, tRPC, Node.js, MongoDB, and Temporal on the back end. It runs on GCP with Kubernetes, managed through Terraform. The agent is currently built on the Vercel AI SDK, and we run an MCP server alongside it.

You don't need to know all of it, but hands-on experience building with LLMs is strongly preferred.

What Your Journey Could Look Like

First day: Get the app running locally and make your first commit. Your onboarding buddy helps you get there.

First week:

  • Meet the engineers, product managers, and designers you'll work with.
  • Learn the agent end to end: its tools, skills, MCP surface, and how we evaluate it.
  • Ship a few smaller features.

First month:

  • Meet the wider engineering team and learn how Ledgy works and how customers use it today. This is the background you'll use for decisions later.
  • Make larger contributions and take a bigger part in code reviews.

First 3 months:

  • Drive part of a larger piece of work, such as process, tooling, a new product, or new functionality.
  • Work with Product and Design to prove and deepen the value AI adds to the product.
  • Take part in architecture and long-term decisions.

After the first 3 months:

  • Take a bigger role in shaping where the team is heading. Own key parts of our AI platform and decide where we can add the most value for customers.
  • Mentor other engineers and raise the bar. Help teams across Ledgy add AI to what they build, whether that means advising, reviewing, or working alongside them.
  • Help shape Ledgy's technical direction, for AI and for everything else we build.

The interview process:

  • Getting to know you (45 min): Meet with someone from our people team to talk about your experience and to ask questions about the role
  • Live Coding (60 min): An equity domain problem to solve collaboratively using your preferred language and IDE. We want to see how you think, so this step does not allow AI. But you can freely look up syntax questions if you need to.
  • System Design (60 min): A system design session where you will design an architecture for a problem from the Ledgy domain using a visual tool of your choice
  • Behavioural (45 min): Answer behavioural style questions about your experience, using the STAR method - with a PM and EM.
  • Culture Interview: A chance to meet one of our founders and your hiring manager for a 30-minute chat about Ledgy's mission and values
  • Offer 🎉

Being part of Ledgy means:

  • Recharge and re-energize with flexible working hours, 25 days of vacation, and up to 40 days of remote work from outside your home country.
  • We make space for your own professional development, with a generous yearly learning & development budget.
  • This role will receive a competitive salary + benefits + equity. All salaries are aligned with competitively benchmarked ranges based on work location and levelling.
  • For candidates based in London we use a hybrid work model of 2 days in the office per week.

Real-world assets, such as the reinsurance fund by OnRe

Built on Solana's high-performance blockchain, Perena is creating a liquid, yield-bearing digital dollar that anyone can access with a sustainable, risk-managed approach.

Looking ahead, Perena is building a full suite of on-chain stablebanking products to expand access to real yield across crypto and traditional finance. The goal is a sustainable financial experience for anyone to transact, save, and invest on-chain.

Perena is founded by a team of builders from the Solana ecosystem with backgrounds in TradFi and DeFi. We believe deeply in pushing financial architecture forward — and in doing it with transparency, resilience, and speed.

Solana co-founders Anatoly Yakovenko and Raj Gokal

Investors from Citadel, Jane Street, IMC, and Susquehanna

Borderless Capital, Binance Labs, Primitive Ventures, Maelstrom, Anagram, Breed, and others

What You'll Do

  • Build and own the frontend applications that bring Perena's financial products to life, from minting and redeeming USD* to portfolio dashboards, yield analytics, and on-chain transaction flows, using Next.js and TypeScript as the core stack

  • Design and implement a scalable component library and design system that ensures consistency, accessibility, and reusability across all Perena surfaces, including public-facing apps, internal operations tools, and documentation

  • Integrate directly with on-chain data and wallet infrastructure, building seamless interactions with Solana programs, wallet adapters, and real-time blockchain state to create intuitive user experiences around complex DeFi primitives

  • Collaborate closely with protocol engineers, designers, and product to translate sophisticated financial concepts (yield strategies, collateral flows, risk metrics) into clear, trustworthy interfaces that inspire user confidence

  • Own frontend performance, reliability, and observability, including optimizing load times, implementing error boundaries, building monitoring and analytics pipelines, and ensuring the app performs under real-world conditions across devices and regions

  • Drive data-driven iteration by instrumenting user flows, analyzing engagement and conversion metrics, and shipping improvements that make Perena's products easier and more compelling to use

  • Experience building and maintaining component libraries or design systems (e.g., using Tailwind CSS, Radix, Shadcn, or similar) with a strong eye for craft and detail

  • Familiarity with wallet integration and on-chain data in a frontend context (Solana wallet adapters, RPC calls, transaction signing) or clear ability to ramp fast

Stablecoins are transforming how the world stores, moves, and grows value — and we're still early. This is a once-in-a-generation shift: from legacy money to programmable, accessible, internet-native finance. Building here isn't just technically interesting — it's globally meaningful.

Fingerprint empowers enterprises to detect and stop online fraud with the world’s most accurate device intelligence. We lead our industry with bleeding-edge identification capabilities and work on turning new ideas and discoveries in the fraud detection space into reality. Our customers range from innovative startups to leading enterprise companies, including Plaid, Dropbox, and Booking.com.

Fingerprint is a globally dispersed, 100% remote company. We were named on on the 2026 Forbes Best Startup Employers list and ranked #803 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of America’s fastest-growing private companies.

We have raised $77M and are backed by Craft Ventures (Tesla, Facebook, Airbnb ), Nexus Venture Partners ( Postman, Apollo.io,MinIO, Druva) and Uncorrelated Ventures ( Redis, Rollbar, Gradle).

The Role in Context

Fingerprint's device intelligence platform processes billions of identification events for some of the world's most security-conscious companies — financial institutions, fraud prevention operators, and enterprises that rely on us to stop attackers. That makes our own application security a product feature, not a back-office function: our customers' adversaries are, by definition, motivated to probe what we build.

As we scale with large enterprise customers, we're investing in application security as a dedicated, first-class engineering discipline. Security is already part of how our teams build — scanning in the pipeline, a Cloud Platform team that treats security as a partner, and a mature compliance posture — and we're now standing up a focused AppSec function, led by a Senior Manager, Application Security who owns the program and strategy, to take it to the next level. You will be the founding senior engineer of that function — the person who turns strategy into a working secure SDLC, finds and fixes what matters, and raises the security bar across engineering through technical depth, tooling, and influence.

This is a hands-on Staff role. You will design, build, and operate — not just advise.


What You'll Do

Secure SDLC & Security Engineering

  • Design and build Fingerprint's secure development lifecycle: security requirements, threat modeling at design time, secure code review, and pre-release security testing — integrated into how engineers already work, not bolted on as a gate
  • Own and operate the security tooling pipeline: SAST, DAST, SCA/dependency scanning, secrets detection, and container/IaC scanning (Snyk and equivalents) — tuned for signal over noise, integrated into CI/CD, with clear ownership and SLAs for findings
  • Build the pipeline AI-first: AI-assisted triage and auto-remediation, security review agents that run inside the coding-agent loop and in CI, and AI-augmented testing — and decide, with evidence, what each is trusted to block, flag, or fix on its own
  • Build paved-road security: secure defaults, hardened libraries and frameworks, reusable patterns (authn/authz, input validation, secrets handling, crypto) that make the secure path the easy path
  • Write code. Contribute fixes, security libraries, CI integrations, and automation directly to engineering repositories

Threat Modeling, Security Reviews & Vulnerability Management

  • Lead threat modeling and architecture security reviews for new products, features, and significant changes across the API, SDKs (web and mobile), dashboard, and data pipeline
  • Run and mature the vulnerability management program: triage, risk-rate, and drive remediation of findings from scanners, pen tests, bug bounty, and customer reports — with clear severity standards and remediation SLAs
  • Partner with the Compliance Lead, who runs the penetration testing program today, on scoping, retesting, and turning findings into engineering work — you bring the technical depth and own remediation
  • Perform hands-on security testing of Fingerprint's platform — manual review and exploitation of authn/authz, API, injection, SSRF, business-logic, and abuse-path issues — with particular attention to the fraud and bot-detection threat surface where adversaries actively attempt to defeat the product

Incident Response & Detection (application layer)

  • Serve as the technical lead for application-layer security incidents: investigation, containment, root cause, and remediation — partnering with Cloud Platform on infrastructure incidents
  • Define what application security logging and alerting should exist, and partner with Cloud Platform and engineering teams to get it built

Security Culture & Enablement

  • Act as the AppSec partner to engineering teams: office hours, design consultations, secure coding guidance, and a Security Champions program that scales your impact beyond one person
  • Develop and deliver practical secure coding training grounded in Fingerprint's real codebase and real findings
  • Mentor engineers in security thinking and raise the bar through code review and design feedback

Partnership & Customer Trust

  • Partner with the Senior Manager, Application Security on the AppSec roadmap: bring technical findings, risk assessments, and recommendations that shape priorities; own execution of the technical program
  • Provide the engineering evidence behind security controls when compliance needs it — you make the controls real; the compliance program is owned elsewhere
  • Support enterprise customer security conversations with technical depth: questionnaires, architecture questions, pen test summaries, and due diligence calls with customer InfoSec teams
  • Contribute to vendor security assessments where third-party code or integrations touch the platform


What We're Looking For

Required

  • 8+ years in software engineering and/or security engineering, with 5+ years focused on application security — you've been the hands-on AppSec engineer at a product company, not a consultant or auditor passing through
  • Strong software engineering foundation: You write production-quality code (TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Python, or similar), understand modern web and API architectures, and are comfortable working inside engineering repositories and CI/CD pipelines
  • Deep practical AppSec expertise: OWASP Top 10 and beyond — authentication and authorization design, API security, injection classes, SSRF, cryptography misuse, business-logic and abuse flaws. You can find these issues by hand, explain why they matter, and propose fixes engineers accept
  • Threat modeling and security review experience: You've led design-time security reviews for complex systems and produced threat models that engineers used
  • Security tooling program experience: You've deployed and tuned SAST/DAST/SCA/secrets-detection tooling in CI/CD and made it useful rather than noisy
  • AI-native security tooling: You've run AI-assisted code analysis, triage, or auto-remediation in a real program — not a trial — and have earned opinions about where it's trustworthy, where it generates noise, and what should be allowed to block a merge. You use AI agents daily in your own security work
  • Vulnerability management ownership: You've run triage, severity rating, remediation tracking, and pen-test programs with real SLAs
  • Influence without authority: A track record of raising security outcomes across engineering teams through credibility, partnership, and good tooling — not mandates
  • Clear communication: You write precise findings and design feedback, and you can explain technical risk to engineers, leadership, and customer security teams alike

Nice to Have

  • Experience in fraud detection, bot mitigation, identity, or device intelligence — the adversarial threat surface here is real and domain-specific
  • Cloud security depth on AWS (IAM, network boundaries, secrets management, workload identity) and familiarity with Wiz or equivalent CSPM tooling
  • Client-side and mobile SDK security: browser security model, anti-tampering, obfuscation trade-offs, iOS/Android SDK hardening
  • Multi-tenant SaaS experience with high-volume, latency-sensitive APIs
  • Bug bounty program operation (HackerOne, Bugcrowd, or equivalent)
  • AI/ML security awareness: LLM-integrated features, prompt injection, agent tool permissions, model and data-pipeline risks
  • Experience with autonomous or AI-augmented penetration testing and attack simulation, and a view on how it complements human-led testing
  • Security certifications (OSCP, OSWE, GWAPT, CSSLP) or published research, CVEs, or open-source security contributions
  • Experience supporting SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls as the engineering owner of the control, not the program owner


The Shape of This Role

This is the senior individual-contributor counterpart to the Senior Manager, Application Security. The manager owns the program, the strategy, and the team; you own the technical depth and the execution. The two roles are designed to work as a pair: you'll bring the findings, the engineering judgment, and the ground truth from inside the codebase, and together you'll decide what to prioritize.

As a Staff engineer, you are expected to operate with a high degree of independence — scoping ambiguous problems, setting technical direction for AppSec, and driving multi-quarter initiatives without needing day-to-day direction. As the founding engineer of a dedicated AppSec function, the patterns, tooling, and standards you establish will be the foundation the practice grows on.

This is not a role for someone who wants to primarily write policy or manage a program from a distance. It's for an engineer who finds real bugs, builds real tooling, and earns the trust of other engineers by making their code better.


Why This Role?

  • Shape a dedicated AppSec function from its first days, with a manager and a mandate behind you — this investment is sponsored at the VP level and prioritized
  • A security problem that actually matters: Fingerprint's customers use us to stop fraud and abuse. The adversaries are real, skilled, and motivated — the threat model here is more interesting than at most SaaS companies
  • Modern stack and tooling already in place: Snyk, Wiz, Cloudflare, Okta, and a Cloud Platform team that treats security as a partner, not an obstacle
  • Your time goes to engineering: Compliance, IT, and infrastructure are each owned by capable teams, so you spend your days on code, findings, and tooling — not evidence collection or ticket queues
  • Staff-level scope and autonomy: You set the technical direction for application security at a company where security is a differentiator in enterprise sales


Compensation & Transparency

At Fingerprint, we believe in pay transparency — it's part of how we operate as a distributed, remote-first team. Salaries are based on function, level, and geographic location, benchmarked against similar stage growth companies.

Because this role is open across the United States and can be based anywhere our team members work from, the salary range reflects that geographic breadth: $177k - $240k

Some example salaries for specific locations are below:

NYC: $209K - $240k

Chicago: $177k - $204k

Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including the successful candidate's location, experience, and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

Due to regulatory and security reasons, there’s a small number of countries where we cannot have Fingerprint teammates based. Additionally, because Fingerprint is an all-remote company and people can join our workforce from almost any country, we do not sponsor visas. Fingerprint teammates need to be authorized to work from their home location.

We are dedicated to creating an inclusive work environment for everyone. We embrace and celebrate the unique experiences, perspectives and cultural backgrounds that each employee brings to our workplace. Fingerprint strives to foster an environment where our employees feel respected, valued and empowered, and our team members are at the forefront in helping us promote and sustain an inclusive workplace. We highly encourage people from underrepresented groups in tech to apply.

jobs.title: Senior Offering Manager - Mainframe Managed Services
jobs.excerpt: At Ensono, our Purpose is to be a relentless ally, disrupting the status quo and unleashing our clients to Do Great Things!
jobs.description:
At Ensono, our Purpose is to be a relentless ally, disrupting the status quo and unleashing our clients to Do Great Things! We enable our clients to achieve key business outcomes that reshape how our world runs. As an expert technology adviser and managed service provider with cross-platform certifications, Ensono empowers our clients to keep up with continuous change and embrace innovation.

We can Do Great Things because we have great Associates. The Ensono Core Values unify our diverse talents and are woven into how we do business. These five traits are the key to achieving our purpose.

Honesty – Reliability – Curiosity – Collaboration – Passion

About the role and what you'll be doing:

Ensono’s Mainframe as a Service (MFaaS) suite is one of the most durable, mission-critical managed service platforms in the market. As we incorporate AI capabilities and next-generation platform innovations, this role exists to evolve and commercialize that portfolio — turning intelligence into offers that customers will buy.

This role is not responsible for defining core AI capabilities. Instead, it focuses on translating existing and emerging capabilities into productized, monetized services — including updating service definitions, pricing models, packaging, and positioning to align with market demand and client value.

You will operate at the intersection of product management, pricing strategy, and service commercialization, ensuring our managed services portfolio evolves from traditional, custom delivery to repeatable, scalable offerings with clear economic models grounded in an AI-First operating model. You’ll set the roadmap, align the stakeholders, and own the outcomes.

Service Evolution & Portfolio Refinement

  • Adapt and evolve existing managed service offerings (e.g., MFaaS) to reflect new platform capabilities (e.g., Telum, Spyre) and AI-enabled delivery improvements such as automation and productivity gains
  • Update and maintain service descriptions, SOW constructs, and feature definitions
  • Ensure offerings remain market-relevant, clearly defined, and differentiated
  • Keep every offering grounded in commercial reality: customer need, market timing, and Ensono’s right to win

Commercialization & Pricing Strategy (Primary Focus)

  • Co-develop and refine costing and pricing models in partnership with Product Pricing and Operations
  • Transition constructs toward standardized, scalable pricing approaches with forward-looking economics
  • Incorporate automation and AI-driven efficiencies into cost-to-serve models
  • Build and maintain pricing frameworks, SKU structures, and packaging tiers and bundles
  • Ensure all offerings are profitable, repeatable, and defensible in the market

Product Packaging & Monetization

  • Productize services into clear, sellable offerings — core vs. add-on capabilities, tiered service levels, and optional enhancements driven by AI or platform features
  • Translate technical capabilities into client-understandable value propositions and measurable business outcomes (cost savings, productivity, risk reduction)
  • Develop standardized proposal constructs and pricing guidance for Sales

Portfolio Roadmap & Lifecycle Ownership

  • Own and maintain the commercialization roadmap across the full MFaaS portfolio
  • Prioritize based on customer impact, commercial potential, and delivery feasibility
  • Ensure every roadmap item has a clear, documented answer to “Why this? Why us? Why now?”
  • Manage the full product lifecycle from ideation through commercial availability to retirement

Vendor & Ecosystem Integration

  • Assess and incorporate third-party vendor capabilities into service offerings, evaluating fit for integration, differentiation, and margin impact
  • Define how vendor technologies are packaged within managed services, priced and monetized, and positioned vs. alternatives (SaaS, ISVs, native tools)
  • Manage product-level relationships with key technology partners to ensure alignment with roadmap and commercial goals
  • Ensure Ensono maintains a cohesive “wrapper” and value layer across vendor-dependent services

Platform Feature Productization (Telum / Spyre / Next-Gen Mainframe)

  • Identify opportunities to package and monetize industry use cases using new platform-level capabilities
  • Translate hardware and software advancements (e.g., embedded AI processing) into new service features, differentiated offerings, and incremental revenue streams
  • Work with Engineering and Architecture to ensure offerings are deployable, operationally supported, and ready for scale

Go-to-Market Enablement

  • Develop and maintain product positioning, messaging, sales enablement materials, and offer definitions for pipeline and deal structuring
  • Partner with Sales to move from point-product or custom solutioning toward outcomes-led selling of standardized offerings
  • Support deal cycles with pricing guidance, packaging recommendations, and commercial clarity

Customer & Market Insight

  • Conduct ongoing customer discovery to validate assumptions, test positioning, and surface unmet needs
  • Monitor the competitive landscape across managed services, AI-enabled delivery, and platform alternatives
  • Turn market signals into roadmap and packaging decisions — not just decks

Cross-Functional Alignment

  • Act as the bridge across Product & Consulting lines of business, Pricing & Finance, Delivery/Operations, and Sales
  • Ensure alignment between what is sold, how it is priced, and how it is delivered
  • Drive consistency across portfolio definitions and commercial models — and drive decisions rather than waiting for them

We want all new Associates to succeed in their roles at Ensono. That's why we've outlined the job requirements below. To be considered for this role, it's important that you meet all Required Qualifications. If you do not meet all of the Preferred Qualifications, we still encourage you to apply.

Required Qualifications

  • 7–10+ years in Product Management, Offer Management, or Service Portfolio Management, with clear ownership of commercial offer development in a managed services or technology services environment
  • Managed services background — strong experience across mainframe, infrastructure, or SRE services, and an understanding of how managed service offers are structured, sold, and delivered
  • Pricing & commercialization expertise — a proven track record of productizing services (custom → standardized) and developing or influencing costing and pricing models
  • Commercial and financial acumen — cost-to-serve modeling, pricing strategy, and margin optimization
  • Translation skill — you turn technical capability into clear packaging and sellable value propositions without losing either the technical or the business audience
  • AI-enabled delivery fluency — enough understanding of automation and AI efficiencies to reshape cost-to-serve and service design (this role applies AI to commercialization; it does not define the underlying AI capability)
  • Cross-organizational experience — you’ve worked across Product, Finance, and Delivery, and can drive alignment between them
  • Clear communicator — you can run a cross-functional meeting across pricing, finance, delivery, and sales and make sure everyone leaves knowing the decision and who owns what
  • Ownership mindset — you drive the roadmap forward, manage dependencies, and don’t wait for blockers to resolve themselves
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent demonstrated experience

Preferred Qualifications

  • Mainframe ecosystem (IBM Z, z/OS, CICS, Db2); IBM LinuxONE experience a plus
  • Infrastructure Managed Services and/or SRE or Application Services
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled delivery (AIOps, automation, developer productivity)
  • Vendor ecosystem familiarity (IBM, ISVs, observability, security, and DevOps tooling)
  • Familiarity with next-generation mainframe platform capabilities (e.g., Telum, Spyre, embedded AI processing)

Success Measures

  • Adoption of standardized, productized service offerings
  • Improved pricing consistency and margin performance
  • Increased attach rates for add-on and enhanced capabilities
  • Conversion of platform innovations (e.g., Telum / Spyre) into revenue-generating services
  • Reduced reliance on custom pricing and one-off deal structures

Role Differentiator

This role is not an AI product strategy role. Success is defined by the ability to take what exists — AI capabilities, platform features, and vendor tools — and turn it into clear, priced, packaged, and sellable services at scale.

Why Ensono?

Ensono is a place to make better happen – for our clients and for your career. You can do great things through innovation or collaboration, by learning or volunteering, or to promote diversity and inclusion. You can do great things for your own health or for a healthier planet. Whatever it means to you to do great things we want Ensono to be the place you can do it.

We are a client-facing business, but we do encourage clients to allow us to work remotely most of the time so if you are not required to be on a client site, you can choose to work from home or in our Ensono offices.

Some of our benefits include:

  • Unlimited Paid Days Off
  • Three health plan options
  • 401k with company match
  • Eligibility for dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life and AD&D coverage, and flexible spending accounts
  • Family Forming Benefit including fertility coverage and adoption/surrogacy reimbursement
  • Paid childbearing and paternal leave
  • Education Reimbursement, Student Loan Assistance or 529 College Funding
  • Sabbatical leave
  • Wellness program
  • Flexible work schedule

As of the date of this posting, a good faith estimate of the current pay scale for this role is $116,000 to 168,000 annually based on a full-time schedule. Please note that placement in the range may vary based on numerous factors including but not limited to skills, experience, internal equity, and business needs. In addition to base salary, other compensation programs, depending on eligibility, include an annual bonus plan based on company and individual performanceand an equity grant under our Associate Equity Appreciation Program

Overview

The Problem Management team resolves complex product issues, serving as the critical link between Support, Product Management, and Engineering. We investigate, diagnose, and resolve issues, document defects with precision, and continuously strengthen the broader support organization through knowledge sharing. We serve customers by bringing clarity, confidence, and technical credibility when it matters most.

The Developer Analyst II is an experienced technical role, well-suited for analysts who have demonstrated strong foundational skills and are ready to take on deeper ownership within specific product or functional domains. In this role, you will conduct advanced toot cause analysis, mentor junior analysts, contribute to knowledge resources, and collaborate with frontline Support, Product Management, and Engineering to drive resolution of complex escalations. You will work with great autonomy while continuing to develop specialized expertise across RealPage’s SaaS platforms.

Responsibilities

  • Resolve complex Tier 3 escalations for assigned RealPage products by performing advanced root cause analysis using SQL queries, API diagnostics, log analysis, and behavioral pattern evaluation.
  • Take ownership of specific product areas or troubleshooting domains within the Problem Management team, developing deep expertise that supports consistent, high-quality resolution outcomes.
  • Document product defects with technical precision and sufficient detail for Engineering review, ensuring clarity of reproduction steps, impact assessment, and supporting data.
  • Analyze escalation trends within assigned product areas to identify recurring issues, systemic gaps, and patterns; share insights with senior analysts and management.
  • Administer escalation tickets in Salesforce with discipline, maintaining accurate case history, customer-facing communications, and resolution documentation in compliance with SLS requirements.
  • Contribute substantively to the team's knowledge base by authoring and updating technical troubleshooting guides, workaround documentation, and product-specific SOPs.
  • Provide peer mentoring and knowledge-sharing to junior team members on troubleshooting techniques, case documentation standards, and product workflows.
  • Collaborate with frontline Support, Product Management, and Engineering to coordinate defect resolution, manage escalation workflows, and ensure consistent customer communication throughout the lifecycle of complex cases.
  • Deliver or contribute to internal training sessions, product knowledge updates, or team enablement activities as assigned.
  • Maintain accountability for assigned case volume, SLS adherence, and documentation quality while balancing competing priorities in a fast-paced escalation environment.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in a technical, analytical, or business field.
  • 4–5 years of experience in technical support, product operations, or a related role, preferably supporting SaaS or enterprise software products.
  • Demonstrated ability to perform root cause analysis and develop actionable, customer-ready solutions using data analysis, product knowledge, and sound technical judgment.
  • Intermediate to advanced SQL skills, with the ability to construct and interpret queries for issue investigation and data validation.
  • Experience with REST APIs, including reading API documentation and executing API requests for diagnostic purposes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document complex technical findings clearly for both technical and non-technical audiences.

KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES

Required:

jobs.excerpt: Bess/PV Engineer BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF SUNSTRONG MANAGEMENT SunStrong Management is a leading independent asset management and servicing platform specializing in residential and commercial solar energy portfolios.
jobs.description:
Bess/PV Engineer


BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF SUNSTRONG MANAGEMENT
SunStrong Management is a leading independent asset management and servicing platform specializing in residential and commercial solar energy portfolios. SunStrong provides end-to-end services including operations and maintenance, customer billing and support, asset performance management, and investor reporting. The company partners with leading capital providers to optimize clean energy assets at scale, supporting the growth of distributed renewable energy while delivering reliable performance and exceptional customer experience

POSITION OVERVIEW

The BESS/PV Engineer is the owner-side technical authority for SunStrong Management's solar PV and battery energy storage delivery portfolio. The role reviews designs, interrogates contractor engineering and test results, and establishes the technical position that Project Managers and gate decisions rest on, across SSM-originated, re-powering, remediation, and inherited in-flight projects, working with EPCs, OEMs, utilities, AHJs, and field service partners.
Project Delivery reports into Commercial Operations by design. The organization that will operate an asset for thirty years sets the standard by which it is accepted at twelve months. A project is not delivered when it is complete; it is delivered when Operations can run it.
The distinguishing expectation is independent technical judgment. The Engineer does not forward the EPC's engineering with a cover note. The Engineer recalculates the contractor's capacity test, finds the protection coordination gap before energization, and recognizes when a battery fire-safety submittal rests on test data that does not match the as-built configuration, and says so in writing.
The Engineer evaluates and recommends. The role does not direct the EPC's means and methods, approve change orders, or make gate decisions; those authorities sit with the Director and the gate owner per SSM-PD-001. Where the Engineer's technical position and a Project Manager's forecast disagree, both are reported and the gap is escalated to the Director.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Design Review & Engineering Standards

  • Lead the technical review of PV and BESS design packages — single-lines, array and block layouts, DC and AC collection, grounding, medium-voltage and protection design, controls architecture, and civil and structural interfaces — against the contracted scope and SSM standards.
  • Verify that design basis assumptions are conservative and traceable — module and inverter derates, DC/AC ratio, clipping, degradation, BESS usable energy, round-trip efficiency, auxiliary load, and availability — and that they match the assumptions behind the performance guarantees.
  • Review short-circuit, protection coordination, arc flash, and grounding studies; confirm that each study describes the equipment actually procured rather than a reference design.
  • Review BESS safety design — enclosure and block spacing, thermal management, fire detection and suppression, explosion control and ventilation, and emergency response planning — against NFPA 855, NEC Article 706, UL 9540 and UL 9540A test data, and AHJ requirements. Confirm that the test data applies to the configuration being installed.
  • Provide the technical content of the operability review of drawing sets against SSM standards — O&M access, equipment standardization against the fleet, monitoring and points architecture, protection and isolation, spares, and maintainability. Operability comments cost nothing at design review and cost a mobilization after energization.
  • Author and maintain the SSM fleet equipment standard, reference design details, and engineering review checklists in partnership with Portfolio Management and Field Service.

Owner’s Engineering & EPC Technical Oversight

  • Review submittals, RFIs, and engineering change requests; return technical dispositions with the reasoning stated, not only the outcome.
  • Define the technical content of Inspection and Test Plans — hold and witness points, acceptance criteria, and required records — for PV, BESS, and medium-voltage scopes; witness factory and site acceptance tests as assigned.
  • Evaluate nonconformances for technical significance and recommend disposition; distinguish a documentation defect from a defect in the installed work.
  • Evaluate the technical basis of change order requests — design deficiency, scope gap the contractor should have caught, or genuine added scope — and provide that evaluation to the Project Manager and Project Controls.
  • Review equipment selection and substitution requests against the SSM fleet standard, warranty terms, and long-term serviceability, including spares availability and OEM service coverage.
  • Reconcile as-built conditions to the design record; where drawings and field conditions disagree, the field condition governs the record and the drawings are corrected.
  • Support the as-is technical assessment of inherited in-flight construction — equipment condition, installed versus designed configuration, and surviving test records — to establish a defensible baseline.

Commissioning, Testing & Performance Validation

  • Review commissioning plans, procedures, and test protocols for inverters, PCS, battery systems, EMS and plant controller, protection, and SCADA before testing begins; recommend acceptance or return with comments.
  • Witness commissioning activities as assigned — inverter and PCS startup, BESS energization and first charge, protection relay testing, and utility witness testing.
  • Independently recalculate PV capacity and performance test results (for example, per ASTM E2848 where contracted) and BESS capacity, round-trip efficiency, ramp rate, response time, and availability results against the contracted test protocol rather than accepting the contractor’s computation.
  • Verify EMS and plant controller behavior — dispatch, state-of-charge limits, ramp and power-factor control, curtailment response, and applicable interconnection and ride-through requirements — against the interconnection agreement and offtake obligations.
  • Validate monitoring end to end with the Portfolio Manager — points-to-points against the SSM data model, alarm verification, and continuous clean data over the validation window.
  • Produce the post-completion performance analysis — measured PI, BESS capacity, and efficiency against expectation at 30, 90, and 180 days. A project is not closed when the work is finished; it is closed when the performance it was built to deliver has been demonstrated.

Performance Analysis, Failure Analysis & Remediation Engineering

  • Support re-powering and remediation scopes with technical scope definition — module, inverter, tracker, and BOS replacement; DC/AC rebalancing; BESS augmentation and retrofit — including the interconnection, structural, and protection implications that distinguish them from new construction.
  • Perform root cause analysis on equipment failures, underperformance, and recurring faults; distinguish defect, design deficiency, installation error, and operating condition, and document the basis to a standard that survives manufacturer and insurer review.
  • Provide the technical substantiation for warranty, performance guarantee, and insurance claims — failure evidence, test data, and loss quantification — in support of the Project Manager who owns the claim.
  • Analyze fleet performance data — production, availability, degradation, battery state of health, and alarm history — and route recurring failure modes into design standards and contractor and equipment selection.
  • Track product safety notices, recalls, code-cycle changes, and the field history of installed platforms; recommend the fleet response.

Safety & Compliance

  • Verify design and construction compliance with NEC, IEEE, UL, NFPA, AHJ, and utility requirements.
  • Support development and review of BESS emergency response plans, hazard mitigation analysis, and first-responder coordination.
  • Provide engineering input to JHAs, PEC/LOTO requirements, and energization sequencing, including stored-energy hazards in DC and battery systems.
  • Exercise stop-work authority without hesitation when design or installed conditions create an imminent hazard. SSM supports every exercise of stop-work authority by owner-side personnel without exception.
  • Support incident and near-miss investigation, including thermal events, with technical analysis independent of the party that performed the work.

Documentation & Technical Records

  • Maintain the technical record on assigned projects — design basis, review comments and dispositions, test records, and approved deviations — so that every position is traceable to evidence.
  • Verify the technical content of turnover documentation — as-builts, test records, firmware and configuration baselines, manuals, and warranty documentation — for completeness, legibility, and attribution; reject incomplete submissions rather than backfilling them.
  • Provide equipment serial numbers, firmware versions, and configuration baselines to the equipment register as construction data lands, so that delivery data reconciles to operations data after turnover.
  • Participate in lessons-learned reviews and route findings back into design standards and contractor selection.
QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering required; mechanical, power, or related engineering discipline considered with relevant experience.
  • Five or more years of solar PV and/or battery energy storage experience in design, owner’s engineering, commissioning, or performance engineering.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license preferred; EIT with a defined path to licensure considered.
  • Working command of PV and BESS system design — string and central inverter architectures, DC-coupled and AC-coupled storage, medium-voltage collection, and protection and controls.
  • Working knowledge of NEC Articles 690, 705, and 706; IEEE 1547 and 2800; NFPA 855; UL 9540 and 9540A; and utility interconnection requirements.
  • Ability to read and interrogate electrical single-lines, protection schemes, civil and structural drawings, and equipment specifications.
  • Direct experience with commissioning and capacity or performance testing of PV and BESS, including independent recalculation of test results.
  • Proficiency with PVsyst or equivalent, AutoCAD or Bluebeam, and familiarity with power-system study software (ETAP, SKM, or PowerFactory) sufficient to review studies. Data analysis in Excel, Python, or SQL preferred.
  • Experience with multiple BESS platforms and EMS or plant controller integration strongly preferred.
  • Experience with re-powering, remediation, or inherited in-flight construction preferred.
  • Demonstrated written precision. Technical positions produced by this role become the evidentiary basis for SSM warranty, claim, and acceptance positions.
  • OSHA 30 and NFPA 70E awareness current or obtainable within ninety days. NABCEP certification preferred.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to travel as needed

  • Comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and 401(k)

About Us:

The Center for Education Market Dynamics (CEMD) is on a mission to improve academic outcomes for underserved students by expanding access to high-quality curriculum and instruction. At CEMD, we work to equip education leaders with the insights they need to make informed, strategic choices about curriculum and instructional materials. We serve as a trusted hub for K–12 education data, making complex information accessible, actionable, and impactful.

We do this by:

  • Developing a comprehensive K–12 dataset to track curriculum selection trends across districts.
  • Sharing insights for the public good to inform strategy, policy, and decision-making.
  • Providing tools and services that help districts and education leaders take strategic, data-driven actions on behalf of students.

CEMD is a fiscally sponsored project of Cambiar Education.

About the Role

The Data Analyst brings their experiences in K-12 education to play a key role in shaping how we turn data into insights, ensuring our work drives impact in the education market. This role leads data analyses and insight delivery, collaborating with Research Managers and supporting project teams to deliver strategic data and solutions to our partners and clients.

What you’ll do:

  • Lead analyses of CEMD aggregated data, from framing the question through cleaning, analysis, and a written summary of findings and meaningful insights.

  • Improve how we collect and validate data, including documentation, QA checks, and reproducible code in GitHub

We are looking for someone with experience in the education ecosystem, who loves working both independently and as a team, to solve complex problems in a role that is a blend of technical proficiency, strategic thinking and effective communication. Additionally, we seek:

  • A curious learner who is not just executing research but actively shaping how it drives impact

  • Experience with creating dashboards using data visualization tools in Tableau
  • Experience with business Intelligence tools such as PowerBi, Tableau, Looker, Quicksight, etc.

  • Experience with version control systems, including GitHub, for code collaboration and workflow optimization
  • Bachelor’s degree with at least 3+ years of relevant experience in data science, analytics or research role

What You Can Expect:

  • A highly-collaborative virtual environment with opportunities to learn from, and with, others across a range of expertise and backgrounds
  • A flexible work culture that is human-centered and supports your growth

jobs.description:
The University of Law is looking for an AI Developer in Education to join our Technology Enhanced Learning and Teaching team and play a hands-on role in shaping how AI is used across the University.

We’re looking for someone who can look at a problem, understand what we are trying to achieve, and then work out whether AI is the right solution and, if it is, build it, test it, improve it and make it work at scale.

You’ll sit at the intersection of AI development, software engineering and education, working closely with our academic and learning design teams to turn ideas into practical AI-powered tools and experiences. You’ll also work directly with our key AI technology partners, helping to shape development priorities, troubleshoot issues and make sure we are getting real value from the technology we invest in.

This is an opportunity to join a University that is actively exploring what AI can do for education, while having the technical expertise and influence to help determine what should actually be built and how it should work.

What will you be doing?

You’ll take technical ownership of the development, configuration and optimisation of AI tools used across our educational provision. This will include:

  • Designing, developing and maintaining Topics, Agents and Workflows within our generative AI platform, turning educational and business requirements into functional solutions.

  • Building, testing and refining AI-powered learning experiences, using user feedback and evidence to continually improve them.

  • Exploring emerging AI technologies and leading technical pilots and proof-of-concept projects — assessing not just whether something can be done, but whether it delivers meaningful value.

  • Integrating AI platforms with University systems, including Blackboard Ultra, student information systems and other digital learning technologies.

  • Working with APIs, LLMs and data integrations to create solutions that are secure, reliable and fit for purpose.

  • Acting as a technical expert for our key AI platforms and technology partners, understanding their capabilities, limitations and development roadmaps.

  • Troubleshooting technical issues and identifying practical ways to improve the performance, usability and reliability of our AI tools.

  • Helping successful ideas move beyond experimentation and into sustainable solutions that can be used across the University.

  • Producing clear technical documentation and guidance that can be understood by both technical and non-technical colleagues.

  • Working closely with academic, learning design and professional services teams to understand their needs and translate them into effective technical solutions.

  • Ensuring our AI development meets the University's requirements around security, accessibility, data protection and academic integrity.

What are we looking for?

We’re looking for someone with a strong technical foundation who is genuinely curious about what AI can do and equally interested in whether it should be used and what difference it will make.

You’ll have:

  • Demonstrable experience developing, configuring and maintaining AI tools or software applications.

  • Strong programming skills in one or more relevant languages, such as Python or JavaScript, alongside experience working with AI/ML technologies.

  • Hands-on experience with LLM APIs, prompt engineering and AI platforms, including chatbot or agent-based frameworks.

  • Experience working with APIs, system architecture and data integration.

  • Strong technical problem-solving skills and the ability to investigate, test and resolve complex issues.

  • Experience communicating technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences and working effectively with a wide range of stakeholders.

  • Experience producing clear, practical technical documentation.

  • A strong understanding of data security, GDPR and technical compliance.

  • A willingness to experiment with emerging technology, while applying sound judgement about what is genuinely useful and scalable.

Experience working within higher education would be valuable, as would experience in a legal education environment, but we are particularly interested in people who can demonstrate strong technical development experience and a track record of turning new technology into practical solutions.

To view the full job description click hereand its associated roles and responsibilities

Why this role?

AI in education is moving quickly. This role gives you the opportunity to be right in the middle of that change.

You’ll have the freedom to explore new technologies, work with AI platforms and technology partners, and collaborate with people across the University to solve real problems. At the same time, you’ll have the opportunity to influence how AI develops beyond individual projects helping us understand what works, what doesn’t, and how successful solutions can be taken further.

If you enjoy building things, solving problems, experimenting with new technology and working with people to turn ideas into something tangible, we’d like to hear from you.

This is a full-time, permanent position and is home-based. Closing date for application is midnight 6th November 2026

Why join us?

Along with a competitive starting salary of £56,000, you’ll enjoy:
